summary: Observation of two bright white lights, initially stationary and then moving silently and slowly: lack of information.
description: On December 31, 2014, at approximately 7:30 PM, a witness noticed two lights in the sky, equidistant, stationary, and silent. After a few minutes, the lights moved slowly and silently over the rooftops of houses out of the witness's sight. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of luminous orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a festive night suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The observed westward movement was very slight, which may be consistent with the weak and unstable, temporarily southwesterly wind recorded in Lille by Météociel. The directions of movement indicated by the witness are not consistent across the different parts of the testimony. Since the witness reports white lights, but Thae lanterns are most often described as yellow-orange, and the wind is uncertain, this lantern hypothesis, while probable, lacks supporting evidence. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information about the wind, pending further testimonies related to it.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a dull yellow ball across the night sky towards the north: lack of information.
description: On December 30, 2014, at 4:20 AM, a witness observed a dull yellow sphere passing north-south. The sphere was quickly obscured by trees. No noise or trail was observed. Only one witness statement was collected. Given the information presented in the investigation report, and pending further details from the witness following our request, the lack of information prevents us from favoring any particular hypothesis. This statement is of average quality: fairly precise and detailed, but old. It is a single eyewitness account with no photographic or video documentation. The observation could be considered somewhat strange; however, the age of the statement prevents us from validly assessing its strangeness. This case is provisionally classified as C, as the observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state, as the significant lack of information prevents us from establishing a definitive opinion.

summary: Observation of a bright white disk in a downward trajectory: observation of the planet Venus.
description: On December 29th at 6:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by a white disc moving downwards in the sky. He took a photograph and asked GEIPAN for an explanation. After checking the photograph to establish the precise time it was taken and to characterize the bright points appearing in the sky, it appears that: - the photo was taken around 6:05 PM, - what the witness indicates as a "star" in the photo is a burned or dead pixel on the camera's sensor, which systematically appears at positions 1774 and 883 (very striking appearance, fluorescent green, and especially present in the same position in subsequent photos (see document: DSC_0003_photo_test_pixel.jpg)). What the witness indicates as "et ea?" while pointing to a large bright point near the horizon is indeed the planet Venus (at that time, no other celestial body besides Venus was visible, except perhaps Mars). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of the passage of a dark triangular shape delimited by lights: probable observation of an aircraft preparing to land.
description: On December 28, 2014, at 6:20 PM, a passenger in a car was intrigued by the presence of two fixed, parallel lights in the sky. As the lights passed over the car, the witness observed through the panoramic sunroof that they formed a dark equilateral triangle, pointing south. The triangle consisted of a light inside each corner and a dimmer light in the center. The trajectory was straight. The witness's description of two, then three, bright lights at low altitude, flying in a straight line southward, and the mention of two flashing lights, point to the hypothesis of a low-flying aircraft arriving from the north (from Great Britain?), preparing to land at Nantes-Bouguenais, approaching from the south, into the wind (see the northerly wind report for Nantes Météociel). Of course, the fact that the witness describes a triangle and not an aircraft seems contradictory to this hypothesis; however, the witness primarily sees the powerful landing lights and, being blind, cannot distinguish the fuselage (see an example in photo DSC_6916_avion.jpg). This is a common perceptual illusion, known as a contour illusion or shape illusion, which gives the impression of a triangle encompassing the points of light. Due to the significant delay after the observation, GEIPAN was unable to access aeronautical information to determine which aircraft was seen. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an aircraft preparing to land.

summary: Successive observations of bright points in the night sky: certain observation of nighttime lighting of wind turbines, the planet Jupiter and public lighting.
description: On December 26 and 29, 2014, the gendarmerie was contacted by two witnesses living in a hamlet in the commune of Nizerolles (03) who were intrigued by the presence of several lights in the night sky (see the investigation report). Based on the evidence gathered, namely: - Testing of regulatory nighttime lights for wind turbines located approximately 12 km from the witnesses and partially visible along their line of sight, confirmed by the gendarmes on site. These lights were the same red color as that noted by the witnesses for two of the UFOs. - Presence of the planet Jupiter, observed along the same line of sight, moving and the same color as one of the UFOs. - Public lighting in a nearby hamlet, confusion noted by the gendarmes regarding witness #1. - Strings of Christmas decorations, also confusion noted by witness #1. - The existence, in one of the witnesses, of a physiological phenomenon of micro-ocular mobility ("micro-nystagmus"). We can conclude that the UFOs observed by the witnesses are very likely various natural or man-made phenomena and objects (Jupiter, red lights from wind turbines, streetlights, Christmas lights, etc.), most of them accompanied by the phenomenon of micro-nystagmus. This case is classified as a certain observation of nocturnal illumination of wind turbines, the planet Jupiter, and streetlights.

summary: Successive observations of the silent passage OE of two red lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 25, 2014, at 12:45 a.m., a witness looking out of a window saw two red lights pass by twice in succession, moving from west to east. No unusual noise was heard. The witness followed the phenomenon until it disappeared from sight towards the Black Forest. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. The observation of red orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a festive night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from west to east, which is consistent with the westerly wind of 11 to 24 km/h recorded in Bele-Mulhouse at 1:00 AM on December 25th (see the Météociel report). However, it should be noted that the wind was very unstable during the night, changing direction several times. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent evolution of 8 luminous points of red-yellow colour in the clear night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 25, 2014, between 1:20 and 1:29 AM, a witness observed the successive movements of eight luminous points in the clear sky. Slightly red in the center and yellow on the outside, these points all moved silently eastward (towards Hyères). No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes along the same trajectory, on a major holiday night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby during Christmas celebrations. The movement is observed from North to East, which is consistent with the unstable North to Northwest wind recorded in Hyères (see the report from Météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as B: very probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two luminous red balls in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: From his garden, the witness observed two luminous, non-flashing, silent red orbs moving slowly eastward before disappearing. The sighting of red orbs crossing part of the sky in a few minutes on a festive night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The eastward movement is consistent with the northwest wind recorded in Niort, according to the weather report. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movements of a bright yellow-fire then white-blue phenomenon in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On December 25, 2014, at approximately 7:15 PM, two people were intrigued by the movement of an incandescent trail in the clear night sky. The phenomenon suddenly disappeared. No unusual noise was heard. A third person in the village also made the observation. Only one questionnaire was collected. Based on the information gathered during the investigation (see the report), this case is classified as a possible B-type observation of a flying object similar to a Thai lantern under specific weather conditions (wind). GEIPAN did not conduct any investigation to identify the source of this trail; therefore, the explanation provided is only highly probable, but not certain.

summary: Observation of two orange lights moving along the same trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns
description: On December 25, 2014, around 1:00 AM, a witness observed two orange lights moving across the sky. The lights followed the same trajectory, a few seconds apart. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a festive night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby for Christmas. The movement was observed from southwest to east, which is consistent with the west wind of 11 to 20 km/h recorded on the Météociel weather service in Reims-Prunay (40 km to the east). The object is probably flying lower than the witness estimates, at around 50 meters altitude, since he already notices quite a few details. The relative blurriness observed is mainly due to the flickering flame and the vapor or smoke emanating from it. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Prolonged observation of a dark object and an orange glow on the ocean: very likely sighting of a boat.
description: On December 21, 2014, at 9:09 PM, a witness on his balcony overlooking the ocean was intrigued by a luminous phenomenon hovering above the water. He observed the glow through binoculars and distinguished a dark object with a lower section shimmering with an orange light. The witness took photographs, but these did not accurately reflect what he observed through the binoculars. At 10:15 PM, the craft glided silently in a southwesterly direction. This testimony is quite consistent: precise and accompanied by two original photographs, but it comes from a single witness. Considering the evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - UFO observed near the horizon. - Visual appearance similar to that of a ship. - Observation of the green starboard navigation light. - Observation of reflections of the ship, possibly its decks, on the water. - Observation direction: towards a busy maritime area. The observation is not particularly strange because the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) is ultimately quite common, both in its appearance and its behavior. GEIPAN (the French UAP research group) considers this case, in section B, a highly probable observation of a boat sailing off the coast of Réunion Island.

summary: Observation in the sky of the movement of a bright yellow teardrop-shaped phenomenon then a matte black circular shape: probable observation of a short contrail from an airplane.
description: On January 21, 2015, at approximately 6:00 PM, three people observed an unexplained phenomenon through their living room window and then on the terrace. Initially, from inside the house, the phenomenon appeared to be a yellow, teardrop-shaped object moving across the sky. The witnesses then went out onto the terrace and saw the UFO, a circular, matte black object that quickly disappeared. The observations were made with the naked eye and binoculars. Only one questionnaire was received, but an on-site investigation allowed for the refinement and correction of certain data (see the investigation report). The strangeness of the observation lay in the juxtaposition of two sequences that, at first glance, seemed unrelated to the same phenomenon. Following the investigators' visit to the site and based on the descriptions provided by the witnesses, it appears that a short contrail from an aircraft is a likely explanation. The three witnesses observed the phenomenon intermittently at nightfall. Initially, the sun's rays illuminated the contrail; in the second phase of observation, the sun's rays may no longer directly illuminate the area of sky traversed by the aircraft. An aircraft contrail can thus rapidly transition from a bright to a dark appearance. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of an aircraft condensation trail.

summary: Observation of a bright object in the sky: probable observation of a star (Vega) above the horizon.
description: On December 18, 2014, around 9:00 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Observing it with a zoom lens, the object appeared to be multicolored and moving in all directions. The witness described a sort of star, larger than average and blinking, which was eventually identified as a very mobile, luminous object, like a kite. The observation lasted an hour. From a location near the train station, the direction of observation was roughly indicated as "above Draguignan," which corresponds to an azimuth of 335° to 360°. It should be noted that the city of Draguignan is not directly visible from this location: the witness's azimuth estimate is probably approximate. The star Vega, a very bright star, was visible at an elevation of 8.4° and an azimuth of 317° at 9:24 PM. Contacted by telephone, the witness indicated that he had seen the same luminous object several nights in a row, in roughly the same location. The observation of a point of light for nearly an hour above the horizon, several nights in a row, strongly suggests the observation of a star. The color changes are due to twinkling caused by atmospheric turbulence; the observed oscillations are also due to twinkling, but also to the autokinetic illusion, a common perceptual illusion when observing a point of light in the dark (see the perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky). As the direction of observation is not precisely known, the identification of the star is not certain. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a star above the horizon; Vega seems a good candidate.

summary: Observation and photography of a luminous oval orange phenomenon in the sky: hoax.
description: On December 16, 2014, at approximately 2:00-2:15 AM, a witness's attention was drawn to a bright light outside. Moving to his terrace, he saw an oval, golden-yellow object moving slowly and silently above the treetops in front of his house. A photograph was taken during the observation, which lasted between 5 and 10 minutes. The object disappeared at high speed, moving vertically away. The image presented as the witness's photograph turned out to be a cropped version of a photograph taken in 1981 by a Mexican photographer named Carlos Diaz (see the full photograph at 1981 the beginning of contact). The witness remained evasive when questioned, providing no details or clear answers to the questions asked (see investigation notes). Given the evidence and the lack of precise answers to the witness's questions, we consider this a hoax. GEIPAN classifies the case as A: hoax.

summary: Brief observation of three bright points aligned in the sky: case not identifiable due to lack of data, although a misunderstanding with stars of Orion's Belt is possible.
description: On December 11, 2014, at 3:35 a.m., a witness closed their window when they observed three equidistant points of light. It was this specific point that intrigued the witness, leading them to suspect a peculiar sighting. Frightened, they didn't look at the sky again until around 3:50 a.m., but the points had disappeared. No other reports were recorded. Due to its lack of specificity and consistency, this case appears to be a possible misidentification of the three stars that make up the asterism known as Orion's Belt. Unfortunately, the lack of data (precise direction of observation, angular spacing between the points of the UFO) and the witness's state of fear at the time of the observation prevent any useful analysis of the case. This case is classified as Class C, meaning it cannot be identified due to a lack of data, although a misidentification of the stars of Orion's Belt remains possible.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 5 red-orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, December 5, 2014, between 7:45 and 7:50 p.m., a passerby was intrigued by the silent movement of five very bright red-orange lights across the night sky. No other reports were received. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes, on the eve of a holiday (St. Nicholas Day), strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from west to east, which is consistent with the light southwest to west wind recorded in Pontoise (see the Météociel report). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a luminous shape of yellow-orange colour on a straight trajectory: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Saturday, November 29, 2014, at approximately 11:15 PM, a person was intrigued by the rapid and silent passage of a luminous, yellow-orange object across the sky. The phenomenon moved in a straight line. No other witnesses were reported. The passage of an orange luminous sphere on a Saturday night suggests a Thai lantern, likely licked nearby after a private party. The witness looked towards the south-southwest; the object moved from their left to their right as it disappeared away. The wind recorded in Le Mans was from the northeast (see the weather report from Météociel). This wind speed is consistent with the direction taken by the luminous object. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the movement in the night sky of 6 luminous grey-white points appearing to form a flat mass: lack of information.
description: On November 29th at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness observed six luminous points crossing the sky from their balcony for less than 10 seconds. The witness reported that these grayish-white points appeared to form a single, dark mass that obscured the stars. The mass disappeared from the witness's field of vision. No sound was heard. Luminous points forming and crossing a portion of the sky in less than a minute on a Saturday night suggest the passage of Thai lanterns. Let's check if the weather report indicates a local wind consistent with the observed movement. The weather report for Caen indicates a light wind, shifting from southeast to north between 10 and 11 PM, then becoming very light and unstable in the middle of the night (weather). It is therefore impossible to know precisely the wind that was blowing at 11:15 PM in Hérouville, very close to Caen, and thus to confirm this hypothesis. Compared to other lantern reports, which most often mention orange orbs, the witness here specifies gray-white dots. The flat, black mass described by the witness is very likely an illusion known as the "illusion of This "contour" is frequent in cases of observing groups of lanterns or triplets of satellites (but at this time, no satellites are visible). Given the uncertainty regarding the wind, and due to the unusual white-gray color, GEIPAN does not have enough information to confirm this hypothesis of thae lanterns, despite strong similarities. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement in the sky of three lights, two white and one red, forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: In April 2015, a witness reported an observation made on November 23, 2014, at 9:40 PM. That evening, from his apartment window, the witness was surprised by the slow and silent movement of three lights in the sky: two white and one red, forming a triangle. The phenomenon followed a straight trajectory. Only one witness account was collected. Given the elements analyzed and reported in the attached investigation, namely: - the light signaling similar to that of an aircraft; - the area frequented by numerous aircraft near Nice Airport; - the movement consistent with the local wind; confusion with an aircraft or with three illuminated balloons or lanterns is possible. However, much angular, azimuthal, and witness data is lacking. We can therefore conclude that, considered as a whole and pending further details from the witness regarding the appearance, movement, position and disappearance of the UFO, this case is provisionally classified as C: observation of a phenomenon not identifiable in its current state, the significant lack of elements not allowing us to establish a solid opinion.

summary: An amateur astronomer observed a luminous ball passing through the eyepiece of his telescope: a probable observation of the Cosmos 1636 satellite surrounded by a cloud of gas.
description: On November 20, 2014, at 9:29 PM, an amateur astronomer was surprised to observe a small, fuzzy, bright sphere with warm tones passing through the eyepiece of his telescope. Of moderate strangeness and with good consistency (a single witness, but with a very precise account), this event turned out to be the observation of the Cosmos 1636 satellite, probably surrounded by a cloud of gas from its remaining propellant tanks, released during an undetermined incident. The UFO's trajectory is indeed perfectly consistent with that of the Cosmos 1636 satellite, and its movement is entirely characteristic of a satellite's motion. However, the hypothesis cannot be confirmed in the absence of any other witnesses for corroboration. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (low brightness of the UFO, observation of a rare phenomenon). This case is class B, a probable observation of the Cosmos 1636 satellite surrounded by a cloud of gas.

summary: Observation of an object following an aircraft: A350 escorted by an aircraft taking photographs.
description: The witness observed an aircraft making a U-turn in mid-air, closely followed by an object positioned between its left wing and tail. Air traffic control was consulted regarding this case: it was indeed an aircraft the witness observed, but a particular one, as it was an Airbus A350 from Airbus Industrie, on a test or demonstration flight, following an atypical trajectory: two loops over the Pyrenees before landing in Toulouse at 12:50 PM. It is noted that Airbus is preparing to deliver its first A350 within the next month. The object observed by the witness was a smaller aircraft, a Corvette, taking aerial photographs (information obtained from Airbus Industrie). It is noted that the position of this escort, south of the Airbus, was well-positioned relative to the sun for taking photos and videos. At the time of the observation, the aircraft was flying at an altitude of approximately 10,000 meters. The escorting aircraft appeared to the witness very close to the Airbus, but it was probably significantly higher than the aircraft, in order to see it from above. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: confirmed sighting of a large transport aircraft on a test or demonstration flight, accompanied by a light aircraft taking photographs.

summary: Observation of several white-yellow phenomena in the form of trails: observation of airplane contrails.
description: The witness is driving on the N13 from Chef-du-Pont to Carentan, heading southeast. He observes a white-yellow "comet-like" phenomenon. The witness reports that the weather is clear, but Meteociel weather reports indicate rain in Cherbourg and showers ending in Caen. The sun rose at 7:45 a.m. in the E-SE (114th parallel), which is slightly to the left of the N13's centerline (approximately 135th parallel). At 8:00 a.m., the witness therefore has the rising sun almost directly in front of him, perhaps obscured by morning mist. The Flightradar24 website (see attached) indicates that at this time several large airliners are flying at high altitude, coming from the west and heading east: an Airbus A330, registration DLH425, and a Boeing 777. The contrails of these aircraft are visible up to approximately 120 km from the observer, where they appear with an elevation above the horizon of around 6°. At this distance, the apparent movement is very small; the contrail appears very short due to perspective, and against the rising sun, it appears yellow, orange, or even red in some cases. See: Strange aircraft contrails. These are the comet-shaped contrails that the witness saw near the horizon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of contrails.

summary: Long observation of the particular movements of a beam of light along the coastline: probable observation of a helicopter (civil security or coastline guards) equipped with a spotlight flying over the coastline of Granville.
description: On November 11, 2014, around 6:00 AM, a witness, from his camper van by the sea, observed a round, luminous white shape moving at first slowly, then accelerating and zigzagging along the coastline. The observation lasted 20 minutes. The phenomenon disappeared over the horizon. Only one witness statement was recorded. After analyzing various hypotheses (see the investigation report), namely: - a boat moving in the Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel; - a helicopter flying at low altitude along the Granville coastline; - an aircraft approaching Granville airport with its landing lights on; - an aircraft flying over the same area with its lights also on, the leading hypothesis is that of a helicopter (civil security or coast guard) equipped with a searchlight. GEIPAN therefore classifies this case as B: probable observation of a helicopter (civil security or cetacean guards) equipped with a spotlight flying over the coast of Granville.

summary: Long observation of the slow movement of bright points in the sky: mistaken for the stars Vega and Deneb.
description: On November 10, 2014, at 10:00 PM, a witness looked out of their window and saw a slightly blinking point of light in the sky. The UFO moved very slowly to the right, while rapidly changing color. The witness tried to photograph the UFO, without success. The observation ceased between 12:45 AM and 1:00 AM. As the witness began filling out an Electronic Questionnaire (EQ) for GEIPAN around 1:40 AM, they looked out the window again and saw the UFO once more. They lost sight of it around 2:30 AM. Only one witness statement was collected. The length of the observation period (approximately 3 hours for the first phase and 45 minutes for the second), as well as the fact that the UFO moved very slowly to the right, are entirely characteristic of an astronomical misinterpretation. Furthermore, the westward movement accompanied by a decrease in the UAP's angular altitude is entirely characteristic of observing a celestial body toward the northwest. If this hypothesis is correct, the UAP observation would therefore involve two different stars, mistaken for a single object by the witness, with the absence of any observation for 45 minutes between 1:00 and 1:45 AM contributing to this type of confusion. The rapid color changes of the UAP (red, green, blue) are also entirely characteristic of observing a bright celestial body, whose light twinkles due to high-altitude winds. A reconstruction using Stellarium for November 10, 2014, at 10:00 PM shows that a remarkably bright star, Vega (magnitude 0.0), was located at an azimuth perfectly consistent with that of the UAP (297th azimuth versus 298th, as estimated by the witness) (see the investigation report). While of moderate strangeness, this case is sufficiently consistent and appears to be a clear case of mistaken identity involving the stars Vega and Deneb, whose positions correspond exactly to that of the UAP at the indicated times. Furthermore, the arrival of a rain disturbance at the time of observation caused high-altitude winds that made the stars twinkle, corresponding to the rapid color changes of the UAP. The small apparent movements perceived by the witness are the result of autokinetic illusion. This case is classified as Class A, a case of mistaken identity involving the stars Vega and Deneb.

summary: Observation of the ballet of several white lights in the sky: observation of a luminous animation on low clouds.
description: silent ballet of several white lights appeared to form a single large object in the sky. The witness recorded a video. This highly unusual observation turned out to be caused by the spectacular light show set up for the inauguration of the Schuman Bridge over the Saône River in Lyon on November 5, 2014 (see The Schuman Bridge Inaugurated). GEIPAN contacted the production company for the show, which indicated that a rehearsal had taken place on Monday evening, November 3, two days before the inauguration. The very particular effects observed by the witnesses resulted from these projections onto low clouds, pushed by the strong southerly wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," meaning explained by a light show.

summary: Observation of the evolution in the sky of a circular object of orange colour and light: lack of information.
description: On November 2, 2014, at 6:25 PM, a witness observed the silent movement of a luminous orange point. It moved in their direction, then changed trajectory before moving away, ascending into the clear sky. Observing an orange point moving slowly in the sky suggests a Thai lantern carried by the wind. In this case, the non-linear movement is not very compatible with this hypothesis, but not impossible given the very pronounced topography of this valley; it is common in valleys to have winds at very low altitudes that are very different from those blowing at higher altitudes. However, it is almost impossible to model, and therefore predict, this wind pattern according to the altitude considered. Furthermore, the weather stations are far from the observation point: Lyon, Macon, Geneva, and they indicate different winds (a strong southerly wind in Lyon, a weaker one in Macon, and a southwesterly wind in Geneva), thus making it impossible to estimate the wind at Matafelon. The photograph shows a pink and blue object, but the witness reports an orange object: due to the shooting conditions (night, camera shake), the shape appearing in the photo is more the result of various imperfections in the shooting process than a faithful image of the observed object. Because of these uncertainties, GEIPAN is unable to provide a justified explanation for the phenomenon; this case is classified as "C".

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three orange objects in the sky: lack of information.
description: On November 1, 2014, at 9:15 PM, a witness observed three round, orange-red objects moving silently across the sky. He eventually lost sight of them. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from the north side of the witness's house, from west to east. This movement does not correspond to the light southerly wind recorded in Melun: weather. This hypothesis of a Thae lantern, consistent with the witness's description, cannot therefore be confirmed, except by considering a gust of wind at the precise moment of the observation. GEIPAN cannot draw any conclusions on this case due to a lack of precise weather data near the observation site and a lack of corroborating evidence. This case of observation of low strangeness is therefore classified as category "C".

summary: Observation of the movement of luminous orange shapes in the sky: lack of information.
description: The observation of luminous orange shapes crossing the sky in less than a minute on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, likely licked nearby after a private party, perhaps related to Halloween. The movement was observed from south to northeast. The wind recorded at Orly Airport was light (4 to 7 km/h) from the south (southeast winds were recorded at Toussus and Pontoise). The witness described a movement towards the north and east, which could be consistent with the local wind, difficult to estimate precisely due to the proximity of the Seine River. However, the rapid movement (12 seconds to cross a large part of the sky) is unlikely to be consistent with a light wind. The observed instabilities could have been caused by uneven local winds. The dynamics of the phenomenon described by the witness are not well-suited to the Thai lantern hypothesis. (See the reconstruction video made by the witness). Due to the lack of precise weather data and the lack of cross-checking, GEIPAN classifies the case as "C".

summary: Two short observations of the rapid and silent movements of a dark triangular object with fixed lights at the corners: high probability of hoax or insincerity of the witness.
description: On October 27, 2014, at 7:54 PM, a witness in their yard observed a dark, triangular object with fixed lights at its corners moving rapidly northeast-southwest across the sky for two seconds. No sound was heard. The witness took two photographs, which they deemed unusable. The witness made the same observation at 11:43 PM, but the object's path was in the opposite direction. No other witness statements were collected. The case was published on February 23, 2016, and classified as Class C due to a lack of consolidated and corroborating information. It is currently under review. The witness's sincerity is seriously compromised by several points (see the investigation report): - contrast processing on the two photos (which the witness attributes to the two successive passages of the UFO on the first evening) highlights the presence of a dark mass (which can be attributed to the facade of a clearly visible building bordering the courtyard opposite the chimney, clearly visible in the photo), and what is described as a moving UFO (and identified as such in the photo by the witness) does not, in fact, move from one photo to the other (as it remains at the same level relative to the dark mass). It is impossible to explain how these fixed lights could have appeared so mobile and fleeting to the witness; - initially, the witness finds nothing in these same photos that corresponds to his observation. The camera was unable to capture the movement despite being set up. Photos unusable. He then sends them to GEIPAN as evidence of the presence of UAPs, without any reservations on his part; - neither the dates nor the times of the photos correspond to those of the two UAP sightings to which the witness associates these photos. The hypothesis of a date and time discrepancy in the camera cannot be considered because the gap between the photos is 3 minutes, while the witness gives UAP sighting times spaced nearly 3 hours apart, specifying the time to the minute (7:54 PM and 11:43 PM). Such precision rules out the hypothesis of an error in memorizing the spacing of the UAP sightings. A misunderstanding between photos cannot be considered either, as these photos are explicitly associated with the sighting since the witness identifies the UAP in them; - the witness does not respond to GEIPAN's request to specify the date of the photos. The only way to explain these inconsistencies other than through a deliberate fabrication of evidence would be if the witness, impressed by their visual observation and so disappointed at not finding any trace of it in the photos, ended up attributing a strange phenomenon found in the photos to the UFO. But this would require that these fixed lights be visible only in photos and not to the naked eye, which is highly improbable. In any case, such a hypothesis would also highlight a lack of sincerity on the part of the witness, given the absence of reservations or questions that such a situation would have prompted, not to mention the lack of response to the GEIPAN email requesting details about the dates and environment in which the photos were taken. This testimony is of average quality: imprecise, coming from a single witness, accompanied by two photographs that do not show the phenomenon, and with unclear shooting conditions. However, its consistency is sufficient to establish the hypothesis of a lack of sincerity on the part of the witness. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes that the available evidence does not provide any physical explanation for the UFO but allows us to maintain the hypothesis that the strangeness most likely results from a lack of sincerity on the part of the witness, not in the fact of having seen anything strange (no evidence allows us to rule this out) but in the testimony given. Classification A: High probability of hoax or insincerity on the part of the witness.

summary: Observation of the silent movement in the night sky of a UFO in the shape of an inverted "Y": probable observation of a flock of large migratory birds.
description: On October 26, 2014, at approximately 1:30 a.m., a witness opening the gate of a house was startled by the silent movement of an inverted "Y"-shaped object. No color or flashing was observed during the approximately 10 seconds of observation. The entire family present witnessed the movement of this phenomenon, which then disappeared from sight. Only one witness statement was collected. Based on the objective evidence gathered in the investigation file (see the investigation report), we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witness could be mistaken for a flock of birds in formation. However, the lack of information and verification prevents us from drawing a definitive conclusion. This testimony is of rather limited reliability, being quite imprecise and lacking in detail, all recounted by a single witness (although it could be corroborated by two other family members) and without a photograph. The observation is actually quite unusual, as it is a UFO with an admittedly uncommon appearance (or shape), but one that is possibly explainable, or at least plausible in terms of shape, size, speed, trajectory, and brightness. GEIPAN classifies this case as B, indicating a probable observation of a flock of large migratory birds.

summary: Observations from an airplane of the rapid passage of a dark teche: probable sighting of a large bird (eagle, falcon, harrier, kite, vulture...) hunting or migrating.
description: On October 26, 2014, a Cessna business jet pilot, three minutes after taking off from Nice Airport at 3:21 PM UTC, reported seeing a dark, rectangular object very quickly pass close to his windshield, following a north-south trajectory at flight level 115. His passenger on his right also saw the object but did not report it. The sighting occurred over the town of Le Bar-sur-Loup (06). Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (attached document), namely: - the plane flew over a protected area housing many species of birds, - among these birds, some are black, large, diurnal and capable of flying at the same altitude as the plane, GEIPAN classifies this case as a Be as a probable observation of a large bird (eagle, falcon, harrier, kite, vulture...) hunting or migrating.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three red spheres on a straight trajectory then forming a triangle in the clear sky: lack of information.
description: On October 19, 2014, at approximately 8:30 PM, a witness and his brother-in-law observed the silent passage of a dark triangular shape with red lights at each end. This phenomenon passed over the garden. These three points moved in a line and then formed a dark triangle. The witnesses left the observation site. Only one witness statement was recorded. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - the possibility that the UFO was not a single, solid object, but rather three independent objects; - the straight trajectory, like that of an object propelled by a steady, constant wind; - the red color, similar to that of lanterns; - the absence of noise; - the duration of the observation, consistent with the lifespan of a lantern. - The observation date was favorable for lantern licking, on weekends, during festivals, weddings, etc. Confusion with a group of three Thai lanterns is possible. However, we lack the azimuthal data for the UFO's movement. This testimony is of weak consistency: imprecise and lacking essential data for analysis (direction of movement), coming from more than one witness and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly unusual, as the objects have ultimately commonplace behavior and appearance. GEIPAN classifies this case in category C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of about ten orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On October 19, 2014, at 10:50 PM, a witness observed 7 to 9 orange lights silently passing across the sky for 8 to 10 seconds. The lights formed a triangle moving along a north-south trajectory. The phenomenon was then obscured by the urban landscape. No other reports were collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from southwest to northeast, which is consistent with the southerly wind recorded at Roissy Airport (20 km). See the Météociel report for the day of the observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Evening observation of a fast and silent passage over witnesses of an elongated and orange shape: probable observation of the landing of a paraglider, possibly motorized.
description: On October 18, 2014, at approximately 10:25 PM, a witness (T1) and his wife (T2) were surprised to see an elongated, orange shape silently pass overhead in less than four seconds, following a straight trajectory. The object obscured the stars the witnesses were looking at. Only one questionnaire was collected (T1). Since the profile drawn by the witness was exactly that of an orange paragliding wing, this was the initial hypothesis considered. An electric paramotor (the only one that allows for instant recovery in case of a problem, such as an engine failure) explains the challenges of launching the paraglider, flying over distances greater than 1 km, and achieving a silent landing (the engine can be restarted just before the final approach). However, a nighttime landing without a moon, without any lighting, without a go-around on final approach, in a field where there are almost always (potentially) horses (animals often terrified by flying wings) is considered downright suicidal by experienced paragliders. Even though this scenario describes an extremely dangerous, even suicidal, situation, no solid argument definitively rules it out, and numerous arguments support it. We cannot speak of certainty because it is very surprising in this scenario that neither the witnesses nor the horses saw or heard the paraglider land at perhaps less than 100-200 meters. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of the landing of a paraglider, possibly motorized.

summary: Observations in nearby municipalities of the presence in the sky of a fixed or rapidly moving luminous phenomenon: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On October 15, 2014, at approximately 10:35/10:40 PM, a female driver (T1) in the town of Vescheim (57) was intrigued by the presence of a luminous phenomenon with fixed colors in the sky. This unidentified flying object (UFO) approached the witness very quickly and silently, frightening her greatly. Upon returning home, she reported her observation to her family and friends and on a social network. A second female driver (T2), independently of the first, reported that while driving in the town of Vilsberg (57) at approximately 11:45 PM on October 15, 2014, she observed continuous lights and a circular shape in the sky, which intrigued her. After reporting the incident to her friends and family and on the same social network as T1, the two drivers made contact. Due to the unusual but highly consistent nature of the descriptions provided by two independent witnesses, the reported absence of aircraft in the area, and the negative results of various investigations related to luminous phenomena produced locally by spotlights or model aircraft, it is currently impossible to substantiate an explanation (see the investigation report). GEIPAN classifies this case as unexplained, in category D1; the large observation distance, the dynamic behavior of the phenomenon without exceptional characteristics, the limited duration of each observation, the fact that the witnesses were constantly moving (even if slowly) and primarily observed through a car window are a set of factors that preclude classification in category D2. The consistency of the testimonies (information and reliability) is good and validates the strange nature of the observation. Should the potential observers present in the car or truck mentioned by the witnesses come forward, the classification may need to be modified. It should be noted that the observation gathered following the appeal for witnesses (published by a newspaper) reinforces the idea that our two witnesses may indeed have observed something unusual. Note: the anomalies reported in T1's car were not observed with sufficient attention and are also shifted in time and space relative to the UFO sighting. Therefore, it does not seem objectively possible (unless further information comes to light) to consider them linked to the sighting. GEIPAN classifies this case as unexplained, in category D1.

summary: Observation of the evolution of an orange light in the sky: lack of information.
description: On October 13, 2014, at 8:50 PM, a witness looking northwest observed for 10 seconds the movements of an orange light coming from their right (see diagram). The light veered 90 degrees to the east, then stabilized before ascending vertically and disappearing. No noise or trail was observed. The witness reported a south-southwest wind of 10 to 20 km/h. The Marignane weather report indicated a light south to southeast wind. Flightradar did not mention any airliners passing north of Pertuis, which corresponds to the start of the witness's observation. Due to the orange light possibly moving with the wind (assuming a southwest wind), one hypothesis considered was that of a Thai lantern nearing the end of its burn: the initial change in direction could correspond to a decrease in the burner's power, causing the lantern to descend. The subsequent perceived movement would then be the extinction of the flame, interpreted as the movement away from a light source assumed to be constant. Given the uncertainty surrounding the wind direction (variable wind, inconsistent weather report from Marignane with the witness's account, proximity to the Luberon mountain range), the unusual day of observation (Monday) for lantern releases, and the complex final trajectory, this hypothesis is too weak to be retained. Lacking photos, videos, or other eyewitness accounts, GEIPAN lacks the necessary information to continue the investigation. This case of observation is classified as "C" due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the silent evolution of a bright white point in the sky; sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: On October 13, 2014, at approximately 6:10 a.m., a driver and his passenger were surprised to see a bright point of light moving in the sky in a comma-shaped trajectory. No trail or noise was observed. The phenomenon disappeared suddenly. Only one witness statement was collected. Given the elements outlined in the investigation report, particularly the lack of a description provided by the Gendarmerie of the object observed above the Nogent nuclear power plant, and pending further information, the lack of data prevents us from concluding in favor of any hypothesis. This case is classified as category C, meaning the observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified at this stage, as the significant lack of information prevents us from establishing a definitive opinion.

summary: Observations of the evolution of a bright red object in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On October 5, 2014, at approximately 10:30 PM, three people observed a bright red object in the sky above the hamlet of Boissezon. The object initially remained stationary, then moved upwards towards Roquebrun. It was subsequently lost from sight to the southeast. Two witnesses reported their observation in a police report. No other reports were filed with the police or the town hall. Considering the objective elements gathered in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - movement with the wind; - color; - brightness; - shape; - duration of observation, we can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses was probably a sky lantern, also known as a Thai lantern. This case is classified as a probable Thai lantern sighting (category B).

summary: Observation of a column of more than ten red lights: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On October 4, 2014, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, a witness observed a column of lights forming an S shape in the sky above a nearby hill, visible from their balcony for 10 minutes. The observation of orange orbs in the sky for a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed to originate from the southwest, which is consistent with the very light and unstable southwest wind recorded in Lyon-Bron (see the weather report). The photos confirm this hypothesis: the complex shapes seen in the photos are the result of motion blur due to the relatively long exposure time (1/4 s). The vertically elongated S-shape corresponds to the upward trajectory of the lanterns, seen along an axis close to the wind direction (the witness's graphic reconstruction seems to poorly match the photos). The lanterns were probably seen beyond the Saône River (near Collonges-au-Mont-d'Or) and are between 400 and 800 meters from the witness (in the first photo). They measure between 40 and 60 cm in diameter. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," an observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a yellow-orange luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern carried by the wind.
description: On October 3, 2014, at 5:28 AM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of a yellow-orange luminous phenomenon (fireball) across the sky. Based on the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely the UFO's movement in the direction of the wind, its dominant yellow-orange color, the impression of a flaming object, its regular movement, and the absence of noise, we can conclude that the witness's observation was likely that of a Thai lantern moving with the wind. This case is classified as a B-type observation of a Thai lantern carried by the wind.

summary: Observation of about thirty red-orange luminous points moving silently in the sky: very likely observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On October 3, 2014, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness left his house and observed numerous shimmering points (about forty in total), reddish-orange in color, moving silently in a linear fashion. The witness had time to take a few photographs before the phenomenon disappeared to the west. Given the objective elements collected (see the investigation report), namely: - Gold color, then yellow-orange or red-orange identical to that of lanterns, - Point shape of the UFOs similar to that of lanterns located at a high altitude, - Behavior identical to that of objects subjected to no or weak wind, - Short observation duration (+/- 1 minute) compatible with the lifespan of lanterns, - Date: a Friday evening, compatible with those conducive to the organization of lantern releases on the occasion of celebrations, - Number compatible with that of lanterns launched in quantity, the GEIPAN in this case has as a very probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: motorist observed a slow and silent movement at low altitude of about ten glowing red halos in the night sky: a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 28, 2014, between 9:02 PM and 9:08 PM, a motorist observed, from his car, the slow and silent movement of about ten twinkling lights in the night sky. All the lights moved in the same direction, at a low altitude, and at the same speed. As they moved away, the witness described them as small, glowing red halos. Other motorists were present and parked on the road. No other witness statements were collected. The observation of orange or red orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from west to northeast (see map), which is consistent with the southerly wind recorded at Roissy (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation). Due to the relatively low brightness of these lanterns, witnesses generally estimate them to be farther away, and therefore larger, than they actually are. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of two flashing red and white lights: observation of an aircraft in a holding pattern for landing.
description: The witness saw two flashing red and white lights approaching from the front in the night. The object turned right, and while the witness went to get a camera, it disappeared. The witness's description of an aircraft with flashing red and white lights clearly suggests an airplane. These very powerful flashing lights were quite blinding, obscuring the green and red position lights (steady and rather dim) and the aircraft's fuselage. The cabin was dimly lit upon landing. Flightradar reports indicate that Turkish Airlines Flight TK1829, an Airbus A321 on approach to Roissy Airport, circled slightly north of Deuil-la-Barre (95), probably to wait its turn to land at Roissy. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of an aircraft in a holding pattern for landing.

summary: round, yellow-orange shape was observed silently crossing the night sky: a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: The witness saw a light in the sky and then observed a round, yellow-orange shape silently crossing the sky in two minutes. The observation of an orange ball crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from the Northeast to the Northwest, which is consistent with the Southeast to Northeast wind recorded in Montauban: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of several colored lights on the horizon: confirmed observation of the nighttime light signaling of two distinct groups of wind turbines and a flare from an Iridium satellite.
description: On September 21, 2014, around 9:00 PM, a motorist and his passengers were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon of unknown nature in the sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the objective evidence gathered (see investigation report), namely: - the color, regular flashing, and immobility identical to the characteristics of the regulatory nighttime signaling lights for wind turbines; - the excellent visibility allowing observation from a significant distance; - the azimuth and elevation profile readings allowing the visibility of the wind turbine lights from the successive positions of the witnesses; - the low angular height. - the illusion of movement accentuated by the absence of landmarks preventing the witness from correctly assessing azimuths, and on the other hand: - the Calsky record confirming the existence of a powerful reflection of magnitude -7.0 on an Iridium satellite, visible from the witnesses' position 1, around the time of the observation - the rapid disappearance, consistent with the short visibility of flares. GEIPAN concludes that the case initially concerns the simultaneous and concurrent observation, towards the West, of the nighttime signaling of a first group of wind turbines and a flare produced by an Iridium satellite, and then, subsequently, towards the Southwest, of the nighttime signaling of a second group of wind turbines. This case is classified as A to A as a confirmed observation of the nighttime signaling of two distinct groups of wind turbines and an Iridium flare.

summary: Observation of a conical drum-shaped object, of extraordinary brightness and evolving slowly in a zig zag before disappearing over the horizon behind trees: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: The witness observed a conical drum-shaped object of extraordinary brightness, moving slowly in a zigzag pattern before disappearing over the horizon behind some trees. The observation of a luminous white shape crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party. The very slight movement was observed to the Northwest, which is consistent with the almost nonexistent (or very light southerly) wind recorded at Orly: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent EO movement of an orange ball in the sky: observation of a Thai lantern.
description: The witness observed an orange ball, which he initially mistook for a planet, but noticed it was moving. He took a video and then saw the object disappear along a vertical trajectory. The observation of an orange ball crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party. Meteociel indicated a light southeast wind consistent with the observed movement: weather. The photos leave no doubt as to the nature of the object (P1050985 and especially 86; the others are blurry due to focus issues or camera shake). But the witness rejects this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" - observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the movement in the sky of a round, red object, seemingly pivoting on itself: probable observation of the movement of a child's ball.
description: On September 17, 2014, around 5:00 PM, a witness observed a round, red object in the sky. The object appeared to be rotating and resembled a saucer. The observation of an object flying in a straight line in the sky, following the wind direction, suggests a balloon, likely a latex or Mylar balloon. The local wind in Nice was from the east, consistent with the object's westward movement (see: weather). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a child's balloon.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky with a curved trajectory: strong presumption of a helicopter in maneuver.
description: On September 17, 2014, at 9:03 PM, a witness observed and filmed a multicolored light phenomenon from their home, which intrigued them. The observation lasted approximately two minutes before the UFO, moving along a curved trajectory, disappeared. No other witness accounts were collected. The weather that day was very unsettled: a wind inversion occurred between 8 and 9 PM. The video shows a light phenomenon with all the characteristics of a helicopter maneuvering: a white flashing (strobe) once per second, characteristic of airplanes and helicopters flying at night. The change in appearance is due to the different faces the helicopter presents during its maneuver, successively revealing one headlight, then two, with its green position light (on the right side of the aircraft). GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group) did not submit the necessary requests to air traffic control in time to confirm this hypothesis. The GEIPAN classifies a slightly strange case in category "B": strong suspicion of a helicopter maneuvering above Bayonne.

summary: Observations of the rapid passage of a luminous phenomenon with a trail in the sky: observation of a large bolide, consequence of the entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid.
description: This phenomenon was reported to GEIPAN by two witnesses in Toulouse and one in Gleize (69). It was recorded by the GEIPAN camera in Toulouse for more than 10 seconds. Seven other reports were received by GEIPAN in the following days. (See attached document: "Summary of observations"). From Toulouse, it was seen crossing the southern horizon from west to east at a relatively low elevation (from 10° to 0° according to the GEIPAN camera). It was noted by numerous witnesses in the Perpignan region and reported by the local press: New asteroid in the Catalan sky. This phenomenon has all the characteristics of a meteoroid (a small rocky body orbiting the Sun) re-entering the atmosphere. The event occurred at an altitude of approximately 25 to 60 km, ending its trajectory over the Mediterranean Sea. This fireball lasted a relatively long time due to its relatively shallow trajectory relative to the Earth's surface; the fireball of September 7th, on the other hand, had a much steeper trajectory. This is not a re-entry of space debris (no known re-entry, and the speed was too high for debris in Earth orbit). This observation is very consistent due to multiple eyewitness accounts and camera recordings. Upon analysis, this case is quite plausible. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of a large fireball, resulting from the re-entry of a meteoroid into the atmosphere.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of clusters of bright yellow points in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On the night of September 13-14, 2014, between midnight and 12:30 a.m., several round, yellow lights were observed in the sky over the Val-de-Marne department (94), between the towns of Champigny-sur-Marne and Créteil. Coming from the northeast, these objects moved slowly and silently in successive waves in a linear fashion. Their number was estimated at around forty. Two eyewitness accounts were collected. This sighting is remarkable for several reasons: - Firstly, because the witnesses reported the sighting to the Air Transport Gendarmerie, which is currently paying particular attention to small objects flying at low altitudes (drones in particular), this case was handled directly by this organization with great care. - The investigation definitively established the origin of the phenomenon: 35 Thai lanterns used to celebrate a civil partnership (PACS). -This lantern-licking event had been authorized by the prefecture, and authorization was granted. Based on the gendarmerie investigation, GEIPAN therefore classifies this clearly identified case as category A: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky then on photographs: direct observation of parhelion, and of flares on the photos a posteriori.
description: The witness was driving when their gaze was drawn to a light source, a sort of second sun. They stopped their car and got out to photograph the phenomenon. The witness observed two types of phenomena (see captioned photo): - With their own eyes, they saw a "false" sun, with an iridescent outline: their testimony is typical of a parhelion located 22 arcseconds from the sun. - In photos taken with their smartphone, the witness later observed luminous "cylinders" opposite the sun: this phenomenon is typical of lens flare, which is a reflection produced inside the lens. It can be verified that these luminous spots are symmetrical to the sun with respect to the center of the image, which explains why they are not always located in the same place in the sky; their position depends on the framing of the sun in the image. This case is class "A": observation of parhelion live, and flares on photos a posteriori.

summary: Observation of a phenomenon with a trail in the sky: observation of an airplane contrail.
description: On September 12, 2014, at 7:50 PM, a witness was intrigued by an unfamiliar phenomenon in the sky. The weather was clear, the sun was setting, and the witness observed something to the west, resembling a rocket, almost stationary at the beginning of the observation, with a V-shaped plume of smoke. Only one witness account was recorded. This type of observation strongly suggests an airplane contrail seen against the light at sunset. Specific information on airplane contrails, published on June 4, 2013, can be found on the GEIPAN website under the News tab: "Strange airplane contrails."

summary: Observation of the evolution of a light grey oval object with a slight white trail in the Marseille sky: probable observation and photograph of an airplane at sunrise.
description: Recent report (December 18, 2015) of an earlier sighting made on September 12, 2014, between 6:00 and 7:00 AM. That morning, the witness's attention was drawn to a bright point of light making circles in the sky before disappearing in a straight line into a cloud. The object was oval-shaped and grayish-white in color. The witness had time to photograph the UFO. No other reports were collected. Analysis of the photos shows a luminous shape preceding a faint white trail: the hypothesis of an aircraft sighting was favored, based on the following factors: - at sunrise and sunset, aircraft are lit laterally: the wing surfaces are in shadow, less bright than the blue sky background, and are therefore invisible. It also happens that the sun reflects brightly off part of the fuselage or windows, creating a very bright point. The resulting shape, visible to the naked eye or in a photograph, can then become a cigar, an oval, or a trapezoid. - The white trail is characteristic of an airplane. Note that the movements described by the witness are surprising for an airplane. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation and photograph of an airplane at sunrise. NB: The witness states that he took the photos around 6:00 AM on September 12, 2014. The time noted in the photo is 8:16 PM: the witness specifies that his camera was not set to the correct time, and that it may have been a little later. Given the brightness of the sky, it must have been around 6:50 AM.

summary: BOLIDE] (NAT) FRANCE (FR) 07.09.2014. Multiple observations of the passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: observations of a large bolide, consequence of the entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid.
description: On September 7, 2014, around 7:00 AM, numerous people in the South of France observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. These observations were reported in the local press. GEIPAN (the French association of astronauts and astronauts) received several eyewitness accounts. This phenomenon had all the characteristics of a meteoroid (a small rocky body orbiting the Sun) re-entering the atmosphere. The phenomenon occurred directly over Catalonia, Spain, at a steep angle (approximately 65°), and between 25 and 60 km altitude. Astronomers believe the meteoroid responsible for this phenomenon was not on a trajectory close to that of asteroid 2014RC, which passed within 40,000 km of Earth on the same day. The two phenomena are not related. This observation case has the highest consistency rating of 1 due to multiple eyewitness accounts and recordings from several cameras. After analysis, this case is very unlikely to be unusual. GEIPAN therefore classifies this case as A: observations of a large fireball, resulting from the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Brief observation of a black line in the sky followed by a bright flash: observation of the volumetric shadow seen edge-on produced by an airplane condensation trail.
description: On September 7, 2014, around 7:00 PM, a motorist spotted a distant, horizontal black line in the clear sky, just above some white contrails left by airplanes, followed by a bright white flash. The witness looked at his road and lost sight of the phenomenon. Only one witness account was recorded. The conjunction in the sky of a black line and airplane contrails is characteristic of the natural phenomenon of edge shadowing. This phenomenon becomes visible when a straight airplane contrail passes in front of the sun and the sun, contrail, and observer are aligned. A shadow is then cast over the entire volume of atmosphere contained within the planar slice containing the contrail, the observer, and the sun. This layer of atmosphere behaves like a slightly tinted pane of glass, imperceptible when viewed head-on, but creating a dark streak when viewed from the side (or edge). This streak is darker the longer the pane, meaning that the straight portion of the contrail is longer. The resulting dark streak is present along the entire height of the witness's line of sight, including the sky. This phenomenon requires precise geometric conditions (witness, contrail, and sun in the same plane). It can therefore appear and disappear suddenly, especially for a witness in a car, as in this case. The bright flash in the sky is probably a reflection of the sun on the aircraft, an intense and brief reflection (the aircraft mirrors the sun), a common occurrence that is rarely noticed except when looking at the sky and other aircraft (as was the case here, because the witness's attention was drawn to the dark streak). There isn't necessarily a link between the two phenomena, just a temporal coincidence. There were several planes at that moment (several contrails), and the reflected plane could have been the one causing the contrail or another. The strangeness that prompted the report is the black trail. We don't have a photo here. Analysis of another report (HYERES (83) 27.05.2016) which includes photos allows for a more precise description of the phenomenon with a detailed account. In this case, it's not possible to provide proof of the explanation, but the probability is very high. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: aircraft contrail (volumetric shadow).

summary: Observation of red-orange lights with different trajectories as they gained altitude, then went out: probable observation of Thae lanterns.
description: Around 1 a.m., a witness observed reddish-orange lights following different trajectories as they gained altitude, then going out. The observation of several reddish-orange lights moving slowly for a few minutes late on a weekend evening strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns. The weather report indicates very weak and unstable winds at that time. The local wind is therefore undetermined, subject to multiple variable influences: this wind regime allows for the almost random movement of objects carried by the wind, according to temporary local breezes. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of two orange balls of light joined by several others: probable observation of Thae lanterns.
description: From the harbor breakwater, a witness observed two bright lights, superimposed vertically. The lights moved randomly and were joined by several others. The witness suspected lanterns. The observation of orange lights in the sky in less than a minute, following the same trajectory, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The lights moved from north to south (towards the sea). The wind recorded in Nice was almost calm. (See weather. The local wind is a very unpredictable local breeze. Due to the witness's description, which is entirely consistent with the description of Thae lanterns, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" – probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a red, bell-shaped object in the sky: lack of information.
description: From a fourth-floor terrace, a witness observed a red, bell-shaped object, seemingly equipped with portholes, moving at a constant speed and direction. Only one witness statement was recorded. This statement lacks information. The statement is brief, and key questions about the object's position in the sky are answered with a question mark. The direction of movement is not indicated, but the constant trajectory suggests a lightweight, non-luminous object (plastic or fabric) carried by the wind, even if it did have the appearance of a "bell with portholes around its perimeter." This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the straight passage of a point of light in the sky: lack of information.
description: On September 1, 2014, at 12:55 PM, a witness, drawn by the sound of an aircraft, observed a bright point of light moving straight across the sky. No other witnesses reported seeing this. The observation of bright points of light crossing the sky in broad daylight can be caused by sunlight reflecting off aircraft or satellites. Flightradar data (attached) shows numerous airliners flying over the witness from NNW to SSE, but not in the indicated direction of Northeast to Southwest. A high-altitude military aircraft not recorded by Flightradar cannot be ruled out. The Calsky data (attached) of satellites flying over the area also lists a large number of satellites, which are presumably invisible during the day. At least four have Northeast to Southwest trajectories consistent with the witness's observation: SPOT4, SPOT5, ARGOS, and KOMPSAT. But these satellites are not known to produce flares in broad daylight like Iridium satellites, although it is not physically impossible. Given these various possibilities, which GEIPAN has been unable to eliminate or confirm, this somewhat unusual case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Brief observation of the passage across the sky of a triangular object composed of non-dazzling white teches: probable bird sighting.
description: On September 1, 2014, between 11:30 PM and 11:40 PM, a witness in his fifth-floor bedroom observed a triangular flying object from his window for a few seconds. The object, composed of six non-dazzling white stars, was moving slowly at an altitude of less than 50 meters. The witness saw the triangular UFO in profile without seeing any "mass" disappear from view above a neighboring building. No noise was heard during this "unexpected" sighting. No other witnesses have been reported. A meeting with the witness was held for a reconstruction and interview (which notably allowed for a more precise determination of the time of the sighting (between 11:00 PM and midnight on the questionnaire)). The description of the UFO(s) (gliding appearance, speed, V-shaped configuration, size, and other elements) strongly suggests an observation of a flock of migratory birds (greylag geese) heading towards the eastern part of Lake Geneva (where there is a bird sanctuary) or of local birds (swans) disturbed by the concert noise that evening. In both cases, the city lights reflected off the plumage, giving the appearance described (see the investigation report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable bird sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent flight of 12 to 15 luminous objects: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness closed his shutters when he observed 12 to 15 luminous objects in the sky, seemingly flying silently in formation. The observation of a group of luminous objects crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from north to south, which is consistent with the northwest to north wind recorded in Bordeaux: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the peculiar movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: mistaken for a satellite.
description: Recent testimony (April 2015) of an earlier observation (August 2014). The witness recounts that on August 31, 2014, between 3:00 and 5:30 a.m., he and a friend observed various luminous phenomena in the sky (shooting stars, airplanes). However, the unusual sinusoidal movement of a luminous phenomenon followed by a "flash" particularly intrigued them. Due to its strangeness and lack of consistency (late testimony with dating errors and imprecise timing), this case appears to be a case of mistaken identity involving one or more satellites. The most unusual observation, involving a flash, is characteristic of an Iridium flare. Unfortunately, the testimony is too late and not precise enough to determine which satellite was responsible for the observation. Initially, the witness did not recognize the UAP as a satellite, as it had a very unusual characteristic: a sinusoidal trajectory. However, the witness, later contacted by GEIPAN (the French UAP investigation unit), eventually recognized it as a satellite and explained that the observed oscillations were due to an optical illusion (nystagmus). Thus, although the exact satellite could not be determined, the case is classified as a satellite misidentification. The case is Class A, a case of mistaken identity involving a satellite.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of approximately 70 luminous objects in the night sky on the same trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 30, 2014, at approximately 11:40 PM, several people observed a large number of luminous (around 70) and twinkling objects moving silently across the night sky. All the twinkling lights followed the same direction, disappearing at the zenith. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness attempted to take a photograph with their cell phone but was unsuccessful. A typical account of a lantern-licking event was given: "It was a bit like a large number of stars had decided to travel together across the sky."
