"Their trajectory, heading north, seemed to be directed by celestial objects. The other objects followed, all forming a coherent whole, which really resembled a flotilla." Indeed, the entire group followed the prevailing wind, which can be meandering in mountainous areas. The general trajectory is consistent with the rather light northerly wind recorded nearby (see the weather forecast on Météociel). It is summer, a weekend night in a holiday destination: all of which is conducive to festive events. The lights of the lanterns are flickering and could also be mistaken for Morse code signals. GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long observation by a single witness of the silent movement of a dark circular mass with light in its center and preceded and followed by several rows of smaller dark mass groups: unidentified phenomenon.
description: On August 28, 2014, at 5:00 AM, a witness observed, for 10 minutes between two thickets, the silent movement of a dark, circular mass with a light at its center, preceded and followed by several rows of smaller, dark masses. Following the investigation, it became clear that this observation did not correspond to the most common misinterpretations (airplanes, satellites, clouds, light displays), although certain aspects of the testimony might suggest otherwise. The case is undeniably strange, but the observed movements were not intentional. The testimony is consistent; the witness filed a report with the police, and a field investigation confirmed their account. GEIPAN classifies this case as category D1: unexplained, consistent, and of medium to high strangeness.

summary: Sighting of two orange lights in the sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness observed and photographed two orange lights in the sky, stationary and appearing very distant. However, the objects disappeared after a few minutes. The observation of two orange lights in the sky within a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The lights, observed towards the southeast, appeared motionless, which is consistent with the almost calm, variable wind recorded in Albi: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Sighting of twelve sparkling red-orange lights in the sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness observed twelve sparkling red-orange lights in the sky, moving randomly. The lights diminished and eventually went out. The observation of twelve sparkling red-orange lights in the sky, moving randomly, on a Saturday night into Sunday morning, especially in August and in a tourist area, suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, often licked after festivals. Meteociel reports a light southerly wind and overcast skies this evening. weather. The information provided by the witness (direction of observation and movement not specified) does not allow us to compare this movement with the local wind to confirm this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B", not very strange, probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of white dot movements in the sky: observation of reflections on airliners, without contrails.
description: On August 22, 2014, at 1:30 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by the movement of several bright white points several kilometers away in the sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. The attached Meteo-France map indicates partly cloudy weather, with very light and unstable winds (Weather). In the observation area (Southwest of Lyon), the weather conditions at that time were such that aircraft only produced contrails between aeronautical levels 357 and 416 (35,700 and 41,600 feet): the multiple aircraft present, recorded by Flightradar24, were flying below these levels (e.g., 24,725 feet), and therefore did not produce condensation trails. The somewhat unusual situation of this cluster of high-altitude aircraft (at least five, see Flightradar report), which were not producing contrails and were likely reflecting sunlight temporarily depending on their position, caused this luminous display that astonished the witness. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of reflections on airliners, without contrails.

summary: Short observation of the silent evolutions of a luminous phenomenon in the cloudy sky: probable observation of a set of lasers impacting the lower cloud layer.
description: On August 22, 2014, at approximately 1:10 AM, a witness was surprised to hear two shouts in the night. Approaching a skylight, he saw, for a few seconds, a metallic-colored disc directly above him, surrounded by small reddish-pink beams of light. The witness followed the silent movements of the phenomenon in the cloudy sky for about 20 seconds in total. No other witness statements were collected. This testimony is quite consistent: precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. Considering the objective elements defined in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - Circular shape of the UFO - Presence of beams - Very high speed - Presence of a cloud ceiling - Absence of noise, we can conclude that the witness's observation was probably that of a set of Skytracker-style lasers, moving rapidly, projected at the base of the low cloud layer. The observation is not particularly unusual because these objects exhibit relatively commonplace behavior. This case is classified as a B-type observation of a set of lasers impacting the lower cloud layer.

summary: Observation of the passage and disappearance of a dozen red-orange luminous points forming a geometric set in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 20, 2014, at 11:05 PM, a witness in a field, preparing to put away his drone, saw a group of 12 red-orange lights in the night sky. The lights, arranged geometrically, formed a moving trapezoidal shape and then went out one by one. Several other people present also observed this. Only one witness statement was recorded. Let's analyze the available evidence: a free-text statement from a witness describing what he saw, and accounts from other witnesses. It is difficult to distinguish between direct and indirect testimony. There is no GEIPAN questionnaire. The police report simply records the receipt of this free-text statement by the gendarmerie. The phenomenon appeared low on the horizon, composed of about a dozen (according to witnesses' estimates) red-orange-vermilion lights "arranged geometrically, forming a kind of trapezoid with a right triangle at its right end." The object in question was thought to be immense (about a hundred meters), delimited by the lights. The witnesses could not see inside the object, suggesting a kind of mist, one of them (who is not the author of this free text) noting "that the stars were invisible through the area delimited by these points of light." The weather situation recorded at "La-Roche-Sur-Yon", approximately 10 km east of the observation points, on Météociel, indicates an average northwesterly wind speed of 7 km/h. These witnesses are influenced by previous observations, including a misidentification of Jupiter and stars that led to a GEIPAN report in 2009. Other insufficiently documented events were classified as C. The witnesses' description of the phenomenon is consistent with the observation of a lantern release during a summer festival. The reddish-orange color and their successive extinction are also characteristic. The description does not explicitly state the direction of movement, but the witnesses' route in following the UFO allows us to reconstruct it. It is consistent with the wind direction (from North) measured at 10 km. Finally, it was a summer evening, conducive to such festive events. The testimony is weak. We have neither a police investigation nor a GEIPAN questionnaire, which is reflected in the absence of any record of the direction of movement. The description mixes a direct testimony (from the author of the text) and reported testimonies unusable by GEIPAN. Nevertheless, given the typical characteristics of lanterns, this lack of consistency does not contradict this explanation; the other possibility could have been that the testimony was classified as unusable. It should be noted that this testimony describes the joy that witnesses can experience from the sensation of having observed "UFOs," a joy all the greater because it fulfills a long-held expectation of seeing one for themselves. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observations of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of the ISS.
description: On Sunday, August 17, 2014, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness observed a intrigued white luminous phenomenon moving across the sky for five minutes. Other witnesses also noted the phenomenon. Only one report was recorded. The witness's description of the phenomenon clearly suggested the passage of a large satellite. A check on Calsky confirmed that the International Space Station (ISS) was indeed visible at that time, in the direction indicated by the witness: from Northwest to East. This clearly identified observation is classified as "A": ISS sighting

summary: Observation of the rapid and straight passage of a large fireball with a short, very bright yellow-white trail in the sky: observation of a bolide.
description: On August 17, 2014, at approximately 9:10 PM, a witness observed, through an open window, the rapid passage of a large fireball with a short, very bright, yellow-white trail. After moving horizontally, the phenomenon disappeared. The observation lasted only a few seconds. GEIPAN, located at CNES Toulouse, about 12 km from the witness, has a camera that is permanently ready to record this type of phenomenon. This camera recorded the same phenomenon at 9:11 PM (See video: the phenomenon is visible in the upper left of the circle, corresponding to the southeast direction). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": confirmed observation of a fireball, also recorded on the GEIPAN camera.

summary: Observation of straight lines at sunset near the horizon: observation of condensation trails from airliners.
description: On August 17, 2014, a witness observed a bright, straight line, followed by several others moving across the sky. He filmed and photographed the phenomenon. The observation of straight lines at sunset near the horizon is characteristic of aircraft contrails. The excellent visibility that day allowed the witness to see aircraft farther away than usual: due to this distance, the contrails appear shorter, slower, and oriented more or less vertically depending on whether the aircraft is moving away from or towards the witness. The appearance or disappearance of the contrail can depend on local weather conditions. The photos leave no doubt about this phenomenon, and the witness is looking in a direction where air traffic is very heavy, especially on a summer Sunday evening. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of contrails from commercial airliners.

summary: Observation of the silent and horizontal movement of a dark, rectangular-shaped object: probable observation of a festive balloon.
description: The witness was in a boat on the Oise River when, on August 16, 2014, at 9:55 PM, he observed a black, rectangular flying object with rounded corners for 10 to 20 seconds. The object disappeared behind the trees. It moved silently in a straight line from Cergy towards Pontoise, that is, from west to east. It was early evening (sunset at 9:03 PM). The Meteociel report indicates a light westerly wind of 6 to 18 km/h (see weather). This observation could be explained by a child's helium balloon carried by the wind. These balloons come in a wide variety of shapes; some can resemble rectangles from certain perspectives. GEIPAN is unable to confirm this hypothesis; however, the date of the observation (end of a summer weekend) is consistent with it. GEIPAN classifies case "B": probable observation of a celebratory balloon.

summary: Observation of the movement of 7 bright points in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness was waiting for the fireworks when she observed seven bright points moving in a cross shape. The phenomenon disappeared into the clouds. The observation of luminous points crossing the sky in formation in less than a minute, on a festive night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns or illuminated balloons carried by the wind, probably released nearby as part of the local festival; one could even consider simple latex or Mylar balloons illuminated only by the lights of the small town. The movement was observed towards the southwest (towards the ocean). The wind recorded in Biarritz (37 km south) was light and from the south: weather. The wind recorded at Biscarosse (70 km to the North) is from the Northwest. The local wind at Vieux Boucou is therefore difficult to determine. On summer evenings, the local wind on the coast is more dependent on sea breezes or thermals than on the general wind pattern, if they are light; therefore, verifying the conformity of the movement of the light points relative to the wind is not possible. The fact that, despite the large number of potential witnesses, there was only one report indicates that this phenomenon was not considered strange by a large part of the population present. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of lanterns or balloons.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of bright orange objects in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Around midnight, the witness saw two bright orange objects in the sky, moving slowly and silently. She then woke her partner. The objects disappeared and were replaced by three others that passed in front of the moon. The observation of a succession of bright orange to yellow circular objects crossing the sky in a few minutes, on the eve of a holiday, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed to be eastward, consistent with the wind recorded in Bergerac: light, from the southwest (see météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of 4 ovoid, white and silent objects in the sky which vanished one by one: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On August 14, 2014, at approximately 9:20 AM, a witness observing the Moon was intrigued by four white, oval-shaped objects clustered together in the clear sky. They appeared stationary and disappeared one by one. No unusual noises were heard during the one- to two-minute observation. No other witness accounts were collected. The witness observed these white, oval-shaped objects in the western sky, showing little movement. The gendarmerie conducted searches for aircraft in the area, which proved negative. Balloons are a possibility: the light northwesterly wind, which was noticeably strengthening (the Mistral was picking up), could have pushed them towards the witness, making them appear almost motionless. Nevertheless, a balloon release on a weekday at that time of day seems unusual, even though it was the height of the summer holiday season. Lacking precise information to support this hypothesis, and lacking cross-checks with other testimonies, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the passage of two bright points following each other in the sky: observation of the ISS and the ATV5 cargo ship.
description: The witness was walking his dogs at 11:25 PM when he observed two bright white points of light moving across the sky at high speed for two minutes. The witness's description of the phenomenon clearly suggested the passage of two satellites, one of them large. A check on Calsky confirmed that the International Space Station (ISS) was indeed visible at that time, accompanied by the European spacecraft ATV5, which was preparing for its docking on August 12, 2014. This clearly identified observation is classified as "A": observation of the ISS and the ATV5 cargo spacecraft.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three bright white headlights arranged in a V and a red headlight in the middle: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, August 9, 2014, at 10:40 PM, a witness in his garden was intrigued by the movement of three large, round, white lights arranged in a V shape and one red light below the clouds. The UFO flew silently over his house, then accelerated and disappeared. No other witnesses reported the sighting. The weather conditions for this observation were as follows: overcast skies, northerly wind, and intense thunderstorm activity without rain (dry lightning): see the attached lightning strike weather map. For your information, at the same time, the International Space Station (ISS) followed by the European cargo spacecraft ATV5 were potentially visible to the north and northeast, quite low on the horizon (see Calsky survey), but the witness was not looking in that direction, and the sky was overcast. He was therefore unable to see this rather exceptional event. Furthermore, the witness's description does not correspond at all to this type of phenomenon. The observation of luminous orbs close together during a thunderstorm suggests a ball lightning phenomenon. The trajectory and behavior of the phenomenon are consistent with this hypothesis, however, some elements of the testimony do not quite fit: the red dot and the relative position of the orbs, which appears stable, may have been due to a perceptual illusion. The reality of the triangle containing the three lights is not certain: it is a well-known perceptual illusion to perceive an object encompassing the outline of luminous points (a so-called "Gestalt" illusion). GEIPAN does not have the means to confirm or refute this last hypothesis (other witnesses, photos), and therefore, this case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Successive appearances of a bright white-blue point in a very stormy sky: probable observation of ball lightning.
description: On August 8, 2014, at midnight, during a stormy period, a witness was intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the clouds. The witness saw a bluish-white point of light that disappeared and reappeared a few meters away in the clouds. The witness's description of points of light in a very cloudy and stormy sky (the witness described at least one flash) likely corresponds to a ball lightning event. GEIPAN has not received the video mentioned by the witness and is unable to confirm the hypothesis, which remains highly probable. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable ball lightning.

summary: Observation of a light in the night sky with a white trail over several hundred meters: probable observation of a flare.
description: At 11:10 PM, a witness observed a light burning out, leaving a white trail in the sky, extending for several hundred meters. The observation lasted 5 seconds. No other witness accounts were collected. The witness suspected atmospheric reentry. A light burning out, leaving a white trail in the sky, extending for several hundred meters, suggests a flare (see a video of a flare). The persistent trail (smoke) is quite characteristic of this type of device; the smoke would have remained visible because it was illuminated by the city lights. The witness, located in the city of Marseille, was observing towards the sea, to the west: in this direction are the Old Port, the MUCEM, and the Frioul Islands (Château d'If). Multiple origins for this type of rocket launch are conceivable: summer festivals, or distress flares (which are typically red) launched from ships. For your information, atmospheric re-entries of space debris do not leave persistent trails at low altitudes. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an illuminating flare.

summary: Observation of the movement of about twenty red-orange colored objects of spherical shape in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness observed about twenty reddish-orange, spherical objects. The objects disappeared behind the houses in the village. The witness suspected Thai lanterns but was unfamiliar with the phenomenon. The observation of orange orbs in the sky on a weekend night suggests Thai lanterns. The near absence of wind makes it difficult to correlate the movement of the objects with the wind. The lack of other witnesses or reports in the press or online prevents confirmation of this hypothesis, which is nevertheless extremely probable. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns released after a private party.

summary: Observation of the silent SW-NE movement of a bright white point in the night sky: observation from the International Space Station.
description: On August 3, 2014, at approximately 10:30 PM, a witness observed a bright white point in the sky moving silently from southwest-northeast to northeast at roughly the speed of an airplane. Only one witness report was collected. The observation of a very bright point of light crossing the sky eastward in a few minutes, less than two hours after sunset, strongly suggests a pass of the International Space Station (ISS). The Calsky website confirms this hypothesis: the ISS "flew" over the witness's area from 10:36 PM to 10:45 PM, from southwest to northeast. As the witness did not mention the ISS in addition to their observation, GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station.

summary: Quick observation of the silent and straight passage of a luminous ball in the sky: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, August 3, 2014, at 1:00 AM, a person was startled to see a fireball silently moving across the sky through a window. Its trajectory was straight. The observation of the phenomenon was very brief. No other witness accounts were collected. The observation, lasting only a minute, of a fireball slowly moving away in the sky on a weekend night suggests a Thai lantern, possibly licked after a celebration. In this case, the proximity of a hall where a wedding was taking place makes this hypothesis highly probable. The witness saw the object fly off towards Saint-Etienne de Crossey, to the northeast. A weather check at the Grenoble-Le-Versoud and Grenoble-Saint-Geoirs weather stations indicated a very light and variable wind, making it impossible to determine the wind direction in this valley area. Despite this entirely plausible hypothesis of a Thae lantern, GEIPAN, due to a lack of cross-checks, classifies this case "C": no other witness, undetermined local wind.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of about ten red objects in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Witnesses observed the silent passage of about ten red objects across the sky at 11 p.m. The observation of red or orange orbs flying in the sky for a few minutes on a Saturday evening strongly suggests Thai lanterns released after a celebration. The Lyon Bron weather report (attached) indicates a very light and unstable wind: it is not possible to estimate the wind direction at that time and correlate it with the observation. However, it is noted that the objects were flying slowly, which is consistent with a light wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage across the sky of a dark object rotating on itself: probable observation of an object carried by the wind.
description: On July 31, 2047, at 8:40 PM, a witness and their family observed a dark-colored object, about the size of a passenger plane, in the clear sky. It moved silently from east to west, slowly, oscillating and appearing to rotate. Sparkling lights were visible. No trails or halos were observed. Only one witness account was collected. This account was quite consistent: precise, coming from three witnesses who knew each other and spoke independently; no photographs were taken. The observation was unusual because the object had an uncommon appearance and unusual behavior. However, its characteristics in terms of speed, size, shape, color, and trajectory did not present any extraordinary aspects that could not be explained. Given the objective elements gathered in the investigation report, this case is classified as B as a probable observation of an object carried by the wind.

summary: Observation of the movement of a triangular object delimited by three luminous balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: From his garden, the witness observed an unknown object consisting of three luminous spheres arranged in a triangle. The three spheres increased in brightness before disappearing as if accelerating rapidly. The observation of orange spheres quickly crossing the sky strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from west to north, which is consistent with the light southwest wind recorded in Caen: Weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Successive observations of the silent passage of phenomena in the shape of a flattened, bright orange rugby ball in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: witness observed a phenomenon shaped like a flattened rugby ball, bright orange in color, moving across the night sky from their apartment (11:45 PM). They repeated the observation three times in a row. The sighting of red-orange balls silently crossing the sky in a few minutes along the same trajectory strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from North to South, which is consistent with the light northerly wind recorded at Roissy Airport (see météociel). The pause observed mid-trajectory could correspond to the object flying over a specific geographical feature: it could be woods or the Fosses Malore hill. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns. The original photos provided are consistent with this hypothesis.

summary: Observation of the movement of white lights in the sky: observation of satellites.
description: The witness, sitting in his garden around 11:15 PM, observed a very intense white light, oval in shape, surrounded by a bluish halo, moving without blinking at the speed of an airplane. The object gained altitude and then disappeared. Other bright spots were seen. The observation for a few seconds of a very intense white light moving at the (angular) speed of an airplane suggests the observation of a satellite during part of its trajectory. The Calsky record (see attached) mentions at that time the overflight of numerous satellites, more or less visible (see the "magnitude" indicator, which is smaller the higher the magnitude). It specifically indicates at 11:16 PM a phenomenon quite rare for a given location: an "Iridium flare," a temporary reflection of the sun on a highly reflective part of the satellite. It is likely that this is the phenomenon the witnesses observed (the questionnaire leaves some ambiguity regarding the phenomenon's position in the sky). Since this reflection of the sun gradually diminishes as the satellite progresses along its orbit and changes its attitude relative to the sun, observers often interpret this decrease in brightness as a sign of moving away, which was the case here. The second part of the observation could correspond to the observation of the two NOSS 3 satellites (4A and 4C) flying in formation, with a magnitude of around 4, that is, like stars barely visible to the naked eye. Their apparent trajectory, as seen from the ground, is a great circle. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": satellite observation.

summary: Observation of the movement of two dark objects in the sky: lack of information.
description: On July 28, 2014, at 9:00 PM, a witness observed and photographed two dark objects moving across the sky above the sea. When they passed directly overhead, he went back inside his apartment, then returned outside to film them. The observation of objects flying in a straight line suggests balloons, such as children's helium-filled balloons, often shiny (made of Mylar), like those found at fairs and carnivals. The witness saw brown objects, but he was facing the sun: any object would appear very dark under these conditions. The doubling of the object could be due to the perspective effect of two balloons, one behind the other. The fleeting point of light could be the reflection of the sun on the balloon, visible only from certain positions of the balloon. Analysis of the photo indicates an angular size on the order of 0.2e, which could correspond to a 70 cm object seen from 200m, consistent with a child's ball carried by the wind. Météociel reports a very weak and unstable wind (see report), and the wind is also variable along the coast (see map): it is impossible to confirm that these objects were indeed moving with the wind, even if their movement (see witness video) seems quite compatible with this hypothesis. Lacking this information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C", but the ball hypothesis is consistent with the observation.

summary: Observation of a black object crossing the sky in a straight line in a few minutes: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, July 27, 2014, around 5:30 PM, a witness observed a passenger plane, then a smaller, black disc moving in the opposite direction and more slowly. The disc became oval and flattened completely as it moved away. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation, against the light, of a black object crossing the sky in a straight line in a few minutes initially suggested a balloon carried by the wind. The Météociel weather report indicated a west to southwest wind, consistent with the eastward movement reported by the witness. What the witness saw must have been a motorized object: perhaps a small circular drone (like a quadcopter) at an altitude of less than 100 meters, operated by someone at the leisure park, or a helicopter at a relatively high altitude, or even an airplane as large as the one the witness observed, but four times farther away. Verifying any of these hypotheses, while consistent with the observation, is virtually impossible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": lack of information or corroboration. Note: The witness made a mistake with the date in their account: they wrote "Sunday, July 28th," when Sunday was the 27th. The weather on July 27th perfectly matches their description (thunderstorm at the end of the day). After verification with the witness, the observation did indeed take place on Sunday, July 27th.

summary: Successive observations on the same evening of the silent movement of luminous white dots forming a triangle in the night sky: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 26, 2014, at 11:10 PM, a couple observed three white lights silently passing by from their garden. These three lights formed a triangle. Three minutes later, the couple saw the same thing again under the same circumstances, but further away from their position. The movement was still in a southwest direction. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness most likely saw Thai lanterns. Indeed, the shape, color, configuration, and trajectory in the sky indicate a lantern release, especially since the observed direction of movement (southwest) is consistent with the wind direction recorded that evening in the region (see the weather report). The date, being on a weekend and/or during the summer, is typical for festive lecher events. Furthermore, a similar observation, supporting the hypothesis of Thai lanterns, was made at the same time nearby (see ovni66). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of several orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Around 11:20 PM, a group of witnesses observed 5 to 7 lights silently flying over a forest before gaining altitude. The objects looped before disappearing. This observation is quite typical of Thai lantern lecher sightings. The red color of the envelope, the group movement, the upward movement and/or movement with the wind (north wind that evening: weather), the disappearance (extinction) after a few minutes, and the day and time (Friday evening) of the observation are all clues supporting this hypothesis. The southward movement (Grigny, Evry) is consistent with the northerly wind observed at Orly at that time. The lanterns likely flew over the Seine and encountered some turbulence during this period. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thales lanterns.

summary: Observation of a straight passage of a red-orange sphere above the road: lack of information.
description: The observation by a motorist at 11:58 PM of a blazing red-orange sphere in the sky in just a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was perceived as being from South to North, the opposite direction to the movement of a car traveling from North to South. This apparent movement is inconsistent with the light northerly wind recorded in Dinard: Weather. It is difficult to determine whether this movement, perceived as the opposite of the car's movement, is real or an effect of perspective, with the object appearing almost stationary during the minute of observation, and probably much more distant than it actually was. The witness refutes this "theatrical lantern" hypothesis. No other testimonies were collected. No atmospheric re-entry of space debris or meteoroids was recorded in this area at that time (sources: aerospace and BOAM). Given this uncertainty (actual movement and brightness), GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information (stationary witness) or corroboration.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness noticed around midnight an orange light moving silently from right to left, followed by several others at intervals of a few minutes. No other reports were collected. The observation of orange lights crossing the sky in a few minutes, following the same trajectory, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed towards the Northeast, which is consistent with the very light, variable wind from West to Southwest recorded in Tours: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of erratic movements of bright points in a night sky: probable observation of satellites and visual illusion (micro-nystagmus).
description: On July 19, 2014, at 11:00 PM, a group of people were stargazing in the mountains. The only witness reported noticing a bright point with an erratic trajectory, followed by other points moving strangely. Some of these points met and merged. Several details in the witness statement support the explanation: - All the UFOs appeared at a single point - Predominantly white in color - Linear trajectory - Disappearance and reappearance a short distance away during their movement. - Erratic movements along small-radius curves. - Acceleration over short distances. - Abrupt stops. The first four points are characteristic of satellites observed at night. The observation conditions are then ideal for observing a maximum number of them: no Moon, high altitude, little or no light pollution, summer sky. Furthermore, the time of observation is also an important factor in that most satellites are visible at the beginning of the night or early morning, still illuminated by the sun and therefore not in the Earth's shadow. The following three points are linked to a natural physiological phenomenon of micro-ocular mobility called micro-nystagmus, little known to the general public, which occurs when one stares at objects, particularly at night. It results in the false impression that bright point objects are affected by small aberrant movements, such as zigzags or brief stops. When it comes to moving objects, detailed physiological explanations can be found in the middle of the page on forum-ovni-ufologie. This phenomenon occurs particularly when the UFO, during its movement, crosses paths with other point-like luminous objects. Thus, the eye, in the presence of a new light source, tries to adapt its night vision as best as possible by focusing more intently on these new lights. The extraocular muscles alternately and rapidly position the center of the retina (fovea) on the light sources and to the side. The brain then misinterprets the information sent by the optic nerve from the retina as zigzags or stops. Note: Testimony from other observers could not be obtained. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies case B: probable satellite observation.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several orange circles in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness was sitting on his terrace when he spotted three orange circles moving slowly across the sky. The photograph of the phenomenon, published in the press the following day in a report from Gratentour, is identical to his observation. The sighting of orange circles crossing the sky in a few minutes, following the same trajectory on a weekend night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed coming from the Southeast (Gratentour), which is consistent with the Southeast wind recorded at Toulouse-Blagnac (South wind at Montauban). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Sighting of two lights in the night sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of two yellow-orange orbs for a few minutes on a weekend night (at 10:45 PM) strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The observed movement was very slight (witnesses in a car, coming from the south), which is consistent with the light southerly wind recorded in Montauban: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of a Thai lantern. At the same time, a similar sighting occurred in Bruguières (31). It could be from the same source.

summary: Silent north-south movement of a group of bright points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of a group of luminous points (around twenty) silently crossing the sky in a few minutes at 10:35 PM on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from South to North. An East wind was recorded at 10 PM in Lyon-Bron: Weather. But a very light, highly variable north to west wind was observed in Macon: Weather. Since Gleize is located between these two weather stations, it is very difficult to confirm the Thae lantern hypothesis based on wind direction. Nevertheless, the witness's description and the number of lights observed leave little doubt as to the origin of the phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of a series of flashes in the sky two days in a row: probable observation of a rapidly rotating geostationary satellite.
description: On July 17, 2014, around 11:00 PM, a witness and his son observed a series of flashes from the sky. The object remained stationary in the sky throughout the 40-minute observation. The intensity of the flashes was comparable in shape and brightness to stars. The witness identified the constellation Scorpius at the Aix-en-Provence planetarium. The following day, the witness and his children were still looking in the same area of the sky, and at 11:10 PM, the family saw the fainter flash three times. Only one witness account was collected. Of moderate strangeness and consistency (several witnesses, but only one account), this case appears to be the probable observation of a rapidly rotating geostationary satellite. Several geostationary satellites are present in the area indicated by the witness, and at least one of them is known to be rapidly rotating. This case is class B, probable observation of a rapidly rotating geostationary satellite.

summary: Observation of a bright point on a very particular trajectory in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On July 17, 2014, at approximately 12:15 AM, a witness observed a bright yellow-orange point in the sky, similar in color to stars, with a very unusual trajectory (straight line, descent, U-turn, ascending zig-zag) before disappearing very quickly. No other witness accounts were collected. Considering the objective elements described in the investigation report, namely the time and duration of observation, the azimuth at the beginning and end of the observation, the good visibility of the ISIS satellite, and the exceptional apparent magnitude of the satellite, as well as the effect of micro-nystagmus (autokinetic illusion), we can conclude that the case likely involves the observation of the star Arcturus, followed by the ISIS 1 satellite. However, one important aspect of the observation does not support this hypothesis; It could be a case of confusion or a false memory, but we have no conclusive evidence to support this hypothesis. This case is classified as C due to a lack of corroborating evidence to confirm the hypothesis of ISIS e, or to confirm the complex movement of the observed point of light.

summary: Observation of successive appearances of yellow-orange balls moving silently in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness observed the full moon at 1:00 AM and saw seven yellow-orange orbs appear successively, moving silently in succession before disappearing. The observation of orange orbs following the same trajectory strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns. The witness described a movement from northwest to southeast, quite consistent with the light wind recorded in Romorantin (15 km away), blowing from the west at 1:00 AM and from the northwest at 2:00 AM (see: weather). The time of the observation, after the World Cup final and on the eve of Bastille Day (July 14th), is very conducive to all kinds of public and private celebrations. The witness, to whom various documents, photos, and videos of Thae lanterns were presented, recognized this type of object (see email), which he was previously unfamiliar with. This case is classified as "A": observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a dark, blurry disc across the cloudy seaside sky: probable sighting of a dirigible or free balloon
description: On July 13, 2014, at approximately 3:15 PM, three members of the same family on the beach at Argeles-Sur-Mer (66) were intrigued by the passage of a dark, blurry disc moving across the cloudy sky. No trail or noise was observed during the 3- to 4-minute observation. The object disappeared as it moved inland. Only one questionnaire was collected. An investigator was commissioned to interview the witnesses. Three key findings emerged from this investigation (see the investigation report): 1. Consistency: This testimony is reliable; any hallucination or vision problems can be ruled out due to the presence of multiple witnesses. Furthermore, the quantity and coherence of the information gathered are good. This case is therefore quite consistent (0.8). 2. Strangeness: The strangeness of this phenomenon is mitigated by the lack of external testimony (0.45). 3. Hypotheses: Plausible explanations were proposed, but we were unable to provide formal proof. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies this case as category B, a probable sighting of a dirigible or free balloon (advertising or surveillance dirigible, or amateur balloon).

summary: Observation of the slow, silent passage of two luminous red-orange balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The witness was in bed, turned his head towards the window, and saw a large, luminous red-orange sphere pass by, connected to a second, smaller one. Their trajectory was slow, silent, and very close (above the roof). The witness observed two luminous red-orange spheres which he estimated to have come from the direction of Sainte-Sévère-sur-Indre towards Thévet-Saint-Julien, that is, from the southeast to the northeast. The objects were therefore following a trajectory from south to north. The weather report from Châteauroux indicates a south wind at 1:00 AM, light and variable, blowing towards the southwest or west (weather). The observed object could have been carried by the wind. The release of Thai lanterns is frequent in the summer on weekends, particularly around July 14th. The witness's observation report supports this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable sighting of Thai lanterns. The witness also refers to a similar sighting, but with several lanterns: it was probably from the same source.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of four blue circles in the sky: lack of information.
description: On July 12, 2014, a witness observed, from their balcony, the slow movement of four blue circles in a group. They began to flash and moved off together, maintaining an equal distance from one another. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (see attached document), the hypothesis of a festive event, without the possibility of confirmation, renders the strangeness of the phenomenon moderate to low. The testimony is of average consistency: imprecision regarding the movement, lack of a diagram. GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to a lack of information or corroboration.

summary: Observation of the silent passage in the sky of 7 to 8 round luminous objects of yellow orange colour: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 12, 2014, at approximately 11:50 PM, a driver and his passenger observed seven or eight luminous, yellow-orange objects silently passing across the sky. The witness had time to take photographs. The observation of these yellow-orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The photographs taken by the witness perfectly support this hypothesis. The movement was observed from north to south. The Geneva weather report indicates a light, unstable wind (north at 9 PM, west at 10 PM, south at 11 PM, and southwest at midnight). Furthermore, in mountainous areas, very localized winds are complex at the end of the day: unfortunately, it is not possible to precisely determine the local wind afterward to confirm whether or not these flying objects were carried by the wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns. See the Meteociel report for the day of the observation.

summary: Multiple observations of luminous phenomena in the night sky: probable observations of atmospheric reentry (shooting star), airplanes and satellites.
description: Between July 9 and July 11, 2014, a witness was intrigued by several observations of luminous phenomena in the sky. The first observation, on July 9 at 11:54 PM, involved a luminous sphere crossing the sky in less than a minute, coming from the southwest. Between 11:45 PM and midnight, a patrol of two gendarmes, located between Le Pouliguen and Guérande, observed a "shooting star-like phenomenon" for two to three seconds, crossing the sky from south to north, eventually splitting in two before disappearing. The descriptions from all the witnesses suggested a bolide (the entry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid, a phenomenon also called a meteorite fall, or meteor, similar to a very large shooting star, but longer-lasting and brighter). The BOAM website (see attached document) does not mention any recorded events of this type, but systematic coverage of this type of phenomenon over France is not guaranteed. One could also consider the possibility of a space debris re-entry, but these phenomena generally last at least a minute. Furthermore, no significant re-entries have been recorded: see: Aerospace. The Space-Track website (see attached document) indicates several re-entries of small debris that day, on highly inclined orbits, which could potentially correspond to the observation (further detailed study is needed). If airplane pilots observed this same phenomenon, they probably found it unremarkable. In any case, GEIPAN has not received any reports. For this first observation, given the high probability that the witness and the police officers saw the same phenomenon, GEIPAN favors the hypothesis of a bolide: atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. Second observation at 12:15 a.m.: a flashing white light moving in a straight line across the sky clearly suggests an aircraft at high altitude: these very bright flashing lights remain the only ones visible from a distance; the navigation lights, quite dim, are not visible, and the eye is blinded by the flashing lights. GEIPAN received the observation report more than a month after the events, which did not allow them to verify it with air traffic control. Third observation: July 10, 11:18 p.m.: the witness describes a very powerful, progressive burst of light lasting less than 2 seconds. This description clearly suggests a satellite flash or flare, which reflects sunlight, like a flat mirror. The satellite's rotation induces this gradual and temporary flare. Many satellites can produce this effect, particularly Iridium satellites. The Calsky website (see attached document) lists several satellites passing directly over Le Pouliguen around 11:08 PM: Helios 1A Rocket, Lacrosse 5. An Iridium flare was also noted at 11:23 PM. Observation at 11:15 PM: this observation of a fast-moving bright ball between the clouds could also correspond to the observation of a satellite, of which there were many at that time. Observation at 11:55 PM: this observation of a bright sphere moving from west to east could also correspond to the observation of a satellite (Echostar 16 could be the source, see the Calsky record). The apparent disappearance of the phenomenon corresponds to the satellite entering the Earth's shadow as it moved eastward. Observation at 0:02: White light with uneven flashing, from Southeast to Northwest. The time and trajectory correspond approximately to the Yaogan 12 satellite (see Calsky report). However, the witness's description could also correspond to an aircraft. Observation at 0:13: The movement of the luminous phenomenon is described in the witness's written report as from East to West, which would be incompatible with that of a satellite. But on the drawing, it is noted as "Northwest," which makes it compatible with the passage of the third stage of the SJ 11-03 rocket. Observation at 0:32: Two flashing luminous streaks and a luminous sphere to the West: This could well correspond to two shooting stars and the large TERRA satellite (see Calsky report). Observation at 0:36: Vertical flash: unexplained. Observation at 12:45 AM: 3 flashes at 5 or 6 second intervals: possible reflections on the Cosmos 1300 Rocket. In conclusion, almost all of these observations, ultimately not very strange, can be explained by the various phenomena that can be observed at night: shooting stars, airplanes, and satellites. This very observant witness had the patience and precision to note everything and report it. The inevitable coincidences between the numerous airplanes and satellites added to the strangeness of the spectacle. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observations of fireballs, airplanes, and satellites.

summary: Observation of the straight, rapid and silent passage of a yellow rectangular shape above the horizon: observation of the passage of an airplane at sunset.
description: On July 8, 2014, at 9:33 PM, a witness was intrigued by the straight passage of a very bright rectangular shape. During the 6 to 8 seconds of observation, the fast-moving object moved silently. No other witness accounts were collected. The witness observed a yellow rectangle moving above the horizon. The sun had set 8 minutes earlier. The witness looked towards the southeast and saw the object pass from left to right (see his drawings). An airplane, illuminated from the side by the setting sun, appeared as a very bright rectangle (the wings do not directly receive the sun's rays; the horizontal stabilizer, being flat, reflects the sun in a different direction than the cylindrical fuselage). The gray halo around the object could be an atmospheric optics phenomenon, quite complex at low altitudes, or a local blinding phenomenon affecting the observer's eye. The Flightradar report indicates a candidate aircraft for this sighting: Air France flight Orly-Marseille on approach to Marignane. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": sighting of an aircraft at sunset.

summary: Observation of the slow, silent movement of orange lights in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: Given the witnesses' descriptions and the elements of the investigation, the hypothesis of sky lantern sightings appears highly probable. Due to the two independent testimonies, the consistency of this case is high (0.8): the reality of the phenomenon is beyond doubt, even if it is not certain that the observations were simultaneous. This could be due to uncertainty about the time of observation, or a second viewing from the same location. The strangeness of the case is low (0.3) because the described phenomenon closely resembles a well-known phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: highly probable observation of sky lanterns, also called Thae lanterns. This case could be classified as A if the potential observers of the lanterns had been identified.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two bright lights in the sky on the same trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: A witness observed a bright light rising from the ground into the sky around 11 PM, then speeding westward. A second phenomenon appeared a few minutes later, following the same trajectory. The observation of bright yellow lights on a Saturday evening, moving successively in the direction of the wind (light easterly wind, recorded in Blagnac: weather), suggests the possibility of licked Thai lanterns after a celebration. Given the relatively low degree of strangeness of this observation, GEIPAN did not request an on-site investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of an orange light point with a stop and sudden disappearance: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: At 10:10 PM, the witness looked out the window and saw a silent, luminous orange point moving away. It stopped moving and then disappeared rapidly. The observation of an orange ball on a Saturday evening, moving with the wind (light southwest to south wind, recorded in Marignane: weather), evokes the image of a Thai lantern released after a celebration. An airplane seen head-on, near landing, can also appear as a yellow or orange ball, but the witness, although near an airfield, is not directly in line with the runways. Furthermore, he is well-versed in aviation. The hypothesis of a Thae lantern is poorly suited to two elements of the testimony: the object stops and then moves off again. However, it is noted that the wind was weak, and the local terrain can create irregularities in the wind. The object disappears at an extraordinary speed: the gradual and rapid extinction of the lantern's flame is often interpreted by witnesses as the object moving away. Given the relatively low degree of strangeness of this sighting, GEIPAN did not request an on-site investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a Thae lantern.

summary: Observation of a fixed orange light between two trees: observation of the star Capella.
description: Early in the morning, the witness looked out of his window and saw a very bright, rather stationary orange light between two trees. The phenomenon disappeared after two minutes. This was an observation of the star Capella, which that night was at an altitude and direction (15°N NE) consistent with the description of a point of light ("star-like appearance") and which "did not move or moved very little." In particular, the low altitude of 15° is conducive to changing colors (flickering). The witness reported the presence of clouds, which explains the disappearance of the UFO after two minutes. The witness indicated a northerly direction, but the configuration of the streets and buildings is more likely to be a skylight facing N NE, and the only large trees between which a UFO could have been seen were located in a N NE direction. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: astronomical observation of Capella.

summary: Long observation of a particularly bright point in the sky: observation of the planet Venus at sunrise.
description: On July 3, 2014, at approximately 5:30 a.m., several witnesses observed a very bright light seemingly floating above a nearby military base. Its shape resembled a crescent. One witness filmed the phenomenon. The prolonged observation of a luminous point moving slowly across the sky suggested a celestial body. The video shows a bright point low on the horizon. A cartographic verification of the observation direction from the Pierre-sur-Haute military base indicated an azimuth of approximately 72° (E-NE). An astronomical verification precisely identified the planet Venus, which was very bright that morning. The shape and varying colors observed by the witnesses are common for this type of observation of celestial bodies low on the horizon; they are the result of twinkling caused by atmospheric turbulence. The witness interpreted this light as strange due to its position above the military base: it was, of course, entirely fortuitous, simply a random alignment, but one that caught the witness's attention. It is often this kind of coincidence that makes a phenomenon seem strange when it would have been perceived as commonplace in another context. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as perfectly identified: the planet Venus at sunrise.

summary: Observation of the movement of numerous white lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thae lanterns or luminous balloons carried by the wind.
description: This high-quality testimony describes the observation at 10:59 PM of a group of white lights (about fifteen) silently crossing a portion of the sky in one minute. The witness describes the gradual disappearance of the phenomenon; this testimony suggests the observation of illuminated balloons or lanterns carried by the wind, probably released nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from East to West (see the witness's diagram). The wind recorded in Colmar at 11:00 PM was light, from the North (Northeast a little earlier): the weather is roughly consistent with this movement. The variability of the wind at low altitude, and the impossibility for the witness to judge the distance or approach of the lights over such a short time, may explain this discrepancy in direction. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thae lanterns or luminous balloons carried by the wind.

summary: Observation by a witness of a phenomenon with three white lights at each end and a red light in the center; buzzing heard: lack of information.
description: On July 1, 2014, at 10:00 PM, a witness, awakened by a noise, observed a triangular-shaped object through his window. It had three white lights at each end and a red light in the center. The witness also heard a buzzing sound. The object appeared to be skimming the roof of a neighboring house. The witness went to get binoculars and a camera, but the unidentified flying object disappeared before he could photograph it. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness's initial thought was that it was a drone. The buzzing sound heard during the observation is consistent with this hypothesis, as is the impression of proximity and possibly the use of lights, which are not regulated for civilian drones. It should be noted, however, that since drone flights over cities are prohibited, especially at night, there is no doubt that no publicity for such a flight would have been given in this scenario. Furthermore, an internet search for the possible use of a drone in the vicinity of Troyes at the date and time of the observation yielded no results. Moreover, confusion with an airplane or helicopter seems unlikely, as the lights did not correspond to aircraft navigation lights. To delve deeper into the analysis, the following information, not provided in the questionnaire, would have been necessary: - the height of the unidentified flying object (UFO) at the time of its first sighting; - the angular size of the UFO; - was the triangular shape perceived or deduced from the lights?; - were the lights steady or flashing? - Photographs of the surroundings, taken during the day, and in particular from the witness's position at their window. A request for clarification on each of these points was sent to the witness by email, but no response was received. The possibility of a drone remains, but due to the missing information, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the straight passage of a white, wingless aircraft, without lights and without a condensation trail in the sky: observation of a passenger plane at sunset.
description: On June 29, 2014, starting at 9:30 PM, a witness was intrigued by the straight passage of a white aircraft across the sky. He didn't recognize it: the witness saw no contrail, no wing, and no lights. But throughout the observation, he heard a muffled sound. The witness took a picture with his phone. It's not uncommon for airplanes not to produce contrails (this depends on local atmospheric conditions: humidity and air temperature). At sunset, an airplane at high altitude is illuminated laterally: the underside of the wings, unlit, is darker than the bright blue background of the sky. Only the illuminated fuselage is visible from the ground. Seen from the ground, it appears cigar-shaped. Furthermore, the flashing (collision avoidance) lights of an airplane at high altitude are never visible from the ground during the day. The Flightradar report indicates a flight from North to South (Airbus A320 Paris-Toulouse AF6168) which corresponds to the observation. This case is class "A": observation of a commercial airliner at sunset.

summary: Observation of the complex movement of several slightly orange luminescent objects in the night sky: lack of information.
description: The observation of orange luminescent objects crossing the sky along the same trajectories within minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The observed trail could be smoke released by the lantern maker. Meteociel indicates a very light north to northeast wind: Weather. The observation reveals two types of movement, only one of which is consistent with this northeast wind. The other movement could be explained by a slightly different wind pattern at altitude, a possible scenario with very light winds, but hypothetical. Although this case has many characteristics of a Thae lantern observation, these complex movements leave doubt as to the nature of the phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Successive observations of the movement of several grey, boat-shaped objects in the sky: probable sighting of kites.
description: On June 24, 2014, at 8:40 a.m., a driver taking her son to school was intrigued by two gray, boat-shaped objects that were stationary side by side in the sky. She couldn't explain what she was seeing to her son. The two objects eventually moved away slowly. On her way home, at 9:08 a.m., she spotted a third object in the same location, moving in the same direction as the others, that is, northeast. This is what the witness described. "Boat-shaped things" most likely resulted from kites. The attached reconstruction positions the locations of the four (reconstructed) observations on the satellite image. These observations from different angles: - allow us to locate the approximate area of the position of the UAPs - show a profile view (observation 1 transverse to the wind measurement) and a front or rear view (observation 3 along the wind measurement) of the UAPs, which perfectly matches an observation of kites in profile and head-on relative to the wind. Although the witness (contacted by telephone 2 years later) refutes this hypothesis, it remains the most probable for GEIPAN, due to the elements described and also because GEIPAN was able to gather information regarding kite flying in a recreational area just upstream (relative to the wind direction, see position in reconstruction). This could have involved users of the area who, exceptionally (the area was inaccessible that day?), decided to fly kites further downstream in the field (of UFOs) or just upstream of this field, so that the witness saw the kites (on one side of the road) without noticing the kite flyers (on the other side of the road). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: kite sighting.

summary: Very brief observation of the presence of several orange lights in the sky and rapid disappearance: lack of information.
description: This account of static orange lights in the sky at 10:45 PM suggests Thae lanterns seen in the direction of the wind. The weather report does indeed indicate a north wind of 15 to 30 km/h: Weather. The other flying object joining this group of lights also moved with the wind. It could be another lantern, launched after the first group. However, the witness's description of this object doesn't quite fit with a Thae lantern; it should be noted, though, that he observed it through his car's windshield while driving, and that the observation was very brief (5 seconds). Due to these rather poor observation conditions and the lack of other eyewitness accounts despite a densely populated area, the strangeness of the case is not established, and its credibility is very weak (single witness, very short observation of 5 seconds). This case is classified as "C": lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the movement and evolution of two orange luminous phenomena in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, June 22, 2014, at 12:55 a.m., a witness, leaving their residence, observed two powerful orange lights moving across the night sky. The witness followed the silent evolution of the phenomena until they were lost from sight. No other witness accounts have been collected. The observation of orange lights crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party, perhaps for the Fête de la Musique (World Music Day). The described shape suggests two lanterns joined together, possibly attached. However, it should be noted that the witness's drawing (two orange circles) does not accurately represent a Thai lantern seen from below: a very bright point should be visible in the center. The movement was observed from the northeast to the west. At Neuilly-sur-Marne (approximately 2 km away) there is a very weak, unstable West wind, passing to the South-East at 2 a.m. (see the report Météociel). The wind recorded at Roissy (20 km north of Noisy-le-Grand) is from the Northeast to North and is light (see the Météociel report). The proximity of the Marne River, at 600m, and the urban environment may explain the change in direction, a consequence of variable wind flow. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of about twenty yellow-orange balls crossing the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of 21 yellow-orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. Their observed movement from northeast to southwest is consistent with the northeast wind recorded in Strasbourg: Weather. The witness reported no wind, but the recorded wind was quite strong, between 20 and 30 km/h. The witness must have been sheltered by houses. The witness had time to take photos and videos. No other reports were collected. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a dark spherical object in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On June 14, 2014, at 8:00 PM, a witness observed a dark, spherical object emerging from a remnant storm cloud. It moved slowly and silently from north to south. The witness recorded a video, but it only shows the object for two seconds, viewed from a distance: a roughly spherical, dark object, reflecting the sun, can indeed be seen. The object then disappears into another cloud. The simplest hypothesis is a balloon, either a thermal balloon or a helium-filled balloon (a small party balloon made of latex, or a larger one made of plastic film). Its relatively slow, linear movement is consistent with this hypothesis. Let's check if the wind direction matches the observed movement: the regional weather readings are as follows in Toulon: West wind 11 to 30 km/h, shifting to the South, weakening (weather and in Cannes: light South wind, shifting to the North (weather). In Le Luc (20 km away), after a late afternoon thunderstorm, a wind was blowing at 8 pm. Weak westerly winds, veering north at 9 PM, very unstable, changing direction every hour (see weather report). We therefore observe weather disturbed by thunderstorms, making it impossible to determine the local wind at that precise moment, at low altitude, especially given the rugged terrain of the region. This balloon hypothesis, while consistent with the observation, cannot be confirmed by the weather data. GEIPAN classifies this case as category "C" due to a lack of verification and cross-checking. The witness refutes the balloon hypothesis.

summary: Observation of the joint evolution of two bright white points in the sky: mistaken for a pair of American military satellites NOSS-3 6.
description: On June 13, 2014, at 12:56 AM, a witness was observing the stars with his new telescope and discovered two bright points moving together (the same distance apart). He then lost sight of it completely in the starry sky. The witness reported his astonishment at the unusual behavior of the UFO. Only one witness statement was collected. The witness provided sketches and a photograph. While the case is of low oddity and fairly consistent (a single witness, but numerous astronomical observations and photographs), it appears to have been a case of mistaken identity involving a particular pair of satellites: a doublet of American military satellites, NOSS-36. The UFO does indeed exhibit all the typical characteristics of such a doublet: brightness, angular separation, trajectory, and timing are perfectly coherent (see the investigation notes). The photograph likely does not show the UFO itself, but only the area where it disappeared. The double star 16 Cygni, appearing here as two closely spaced points, was certainly interpreted by the witness as the UAP. The UAP's periods of inactivity can be explained by the discontinuity of the observation: the UAP's temporary disappearance due to the brightness of the Moon and the presence of numerous stars. This case is Class A, mistaken for the pair of American military satellites NOSS-3 (A) and (B).

summary: Observation of orange luminous phenomena in the sky: observation of contrails from airplanes at sunset.
description: On June 12, 2014, at 10:15 PM, a witness observed and photographed two orange luminous phenomena in the sky. The photos clearly resemble contrails, made very bright by the setting sun. The sun was nearly 3 arcseconds below the horizon, having set at 9:57 PM, less than 20 minutes before the observation. At an altitude of 10,000 meters, the minimum cruising altitude for medium and long-haul flights, the sun was still visible. The aircraft was moving away from the observer towards the Northwest, in the direction of the setting sun: the contrail was actually parallel to the Earth, but viewed from below, at a shallow angle of incidence, it appeared vertical. See an explanation Strange airplane contrails. These two parallel trails, which change direction together, suggest two military aircraft rather than two airliners. GEIPAN was unable to gather the necessary information in time to resolve this uncertainty. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of airplane condensation trails.

summary: Intermittent observation of a white, flat, saucer-shaped phenomenon below at low altitude: lack of information.
description: On June 11, 2014, at approximately 7:45 PM, a motorist driving alone was surprised to see a fairly large white object at low altitude, directly in line with the road (east or southeast). He likened its shape to that of a flying saucer with a flat underside. Continuing on his way, he lost sight of the object, which was hidden by trees, but spotted it again a few kilometers later as a tiny dot in the sky. Only one eyewitness account was collected for this phenomenon. The UFO was visible directly in line with the road, that is, to the east or southeast. Several hypotheses have been put forward (see the investigation notes). The hypothesis of mistaking the moon for the moonrise was investigated: clear weather, the UFO very low on the horizon and constantly moving away from the witness, and the time close to the time indicated for the observation. Furthermore, it should be noted that with an azimuth of 116°, the Moon was visible along the D25 road at the roundabout where the witness spotted the UFO. However, the lack of precision (absence of a direction during the last phase of observation) prevents formal confirmation of the hypothesis of mistaking the Moon for the other. Of moderate strangeness and weak consistency (single witness, no photograph, late testimony), this case proves too imprecise to be identified. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of their observation based on their feelings (astonishment, excitement, observation while driving). This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of precision.

summary: Observation of a gigantic blue-grey circle around the sun during the day: observation of a solar halo.
description: On Sunday, June 8, 2014, between 1:00 and 2:00 PM, a witness observed and photographed a gigantic blue-gray circle around the sun. This observation is typical of a halo phenomenon, which occurs under specific atmospheric conditions. See: Solar halo. A small bright spot is also visible in the photo in the upper left corner, inside the halo; this is a stray reflection of the sun produced by the camera's lens. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: solar halo.

summary: Observation of about twenty lights in the night sky which gradually went out: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of a group of orange orbs (about twenty according to the witness), for a few minutes on a Friday evening at 11:53 PM, suggests a Thae lantern release following a festival. The witness observed the orbs almost stationary, moving very slightly to their left and weakening: the lanterns, pushed by the wind, were moving away from the witness, slightly to the west. Meteociel reported a light west or northwest wind of 13 to 19 km/h at Roissy: Weather. No other reports were collected. This case is classified as "B" – probable observation of Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of several bright objects in the sky: probable observations of satellites and the International Space Station.
description: On June 7, 2014, between 2:00 and 4:00 AM, a person was surprised and intrigued by the observation of luminous phenomena in the night sky. The observation unfolded in three phases: - Just after 2:30 AM: three objects moving from south to north: according to Calsky (see report), several satellites were candidates at this time: IGS02, Cosmos 1782 Rocket, and NOS 3-6 Rocket. - Two blinking objects moving from south to northwest, and from north to south: according to Calsky, several satellites could have followed this trajectory. The blinking could be explained by the fact that some satellites are rotating and reflecting sunlight irregularly. They could also be aircraft, as their anti-collision lights blink once per second. - A "gigantic" light after 3:15 AM, observed in the west and disappearing towards the south. Calsky reports that the ISS passed overhead that day, visible from 3:16 AM at its rising in the West (WNW) until 3:22 AM when it disappeared towards the South (SE). It is, however, surprising that the witness used the word "gigantic" for a light as bright as the planet Venus: the fact that the observation took place in the middle of the night may explain this. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of satellites and the International Space Station (ISS). The middle of the night is conducive to over-interpretation of celestial phenomena, particularly for emotional people, which seems to be the case with this witness.

summary: Successive observations of colored luminous spheres in the starry sky with binoculars and a telescope: probable observation of particularly sparkling stars at low elevation.
description: From June 2014 to December 2015, an individual regularly observed the sky with binoculars and a telescope and reported several sightings of colored spheres, visible only on starry nights. The multicolored spheres moved slightly. The witness specifically recounted a long observation made on June 6, 2014. No other accounts were collected. The long (30-minute) and repeated observation of luminous points in the sky, moving slowly and appearing multicolored when viewed with binoculars or a telescope, suggests the observation of stars, particularly twinkling at low elevations. Based on the star chart from the time of the observation, these could be Capella, Vega, or Deneb. The effect observed by the witness may be the result of an incorrect adjustment of the telescope. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of particularly sparkling stars at low elevation.

summary: Observations of the silent passage of a luminous red-orange ball in the sky: lack of information.
description: On Monday, June 2, 2014, at approximately 10:45 PM, three friends observed a reddish-orange sphere moving at a constant speed across the clear sky. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted three to four minutes. This report of a significant glow, seemingly a fireball, lasting three to four minutes, suggests a Thai lantern carried by the wind. The Météociel weather report from Besançon indicated a very light northerly wind.
