However, lantern releases during the week are rare, and the fact that this luminous object was unique does not support this hypothesis. The weak and unstable wind also does not confirm that the object was moving with the wind. The relative unfamiliarity of the case (similarity to a known phenomenon), and the delay of more than eight months between the event and its receipt by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Astronomical Phenomena), do not justify a field investigation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent movement of three bright points across the sky: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteor.
description: On June 1, 2014, at 11:00 PM, a witness observed an object silently crossing the sky at very high speed, appearing as three bright points. The description of the UFO, typical of a fireball, leaves little doubt that it was a case of mistaken identity. Of moderate strangeness and consistency (single witness), this case appears to be a probable case of mistaken identity with a well-known astronomical phenomenon: a meteor. It should be noted that a meteor was recorded by an amateur astronomy network at a time close to that of the observation, but its trajectory is inconsistent. An independent account published online nevertheless presents strong similarities with the UFO observation. This case is classified as Class B, probable mistaken identity with a fireball. A similar observation was also noted, within minutes, in Étrelles (35): see that case.

summary: Observations in the night sky of a dark mass, equipped with two small lights. Sudden movement at dizzying speed and disappearance: unexplained case of a strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: Witnesses, in a company car, quickly observed a dark mass in the sky, equipped with two small, dim lights. The mass suddenly moved at a dizzying speed and disappeared. A field investigation confirmed the witnesses' reports and considered several hypotheses (see the investigation report), but none fully fit the observations. In conclusion, this was an unidentified phenomenon (UAP), observed by two highly reliable witnesses under ideal viewing conditions, and which seems to defy all hypotheses, particularly the explanation of a meteor (fireball). However, the uncertainty surrounding the UAP's trajectory, its very brief nature, and the interdependence of the two witnesses who immediately shared their observations preclude classification as a D2 event, in the absence of photographs or videos. GEIPAN classifies this case D1 as an unexplained case, of high consistency due to the two high-quality testimonies, and of medium strangeness (the materiality of the object is possible but not certain).

summary: Observation of a set of bright orange points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of a group of orange orbs around 11 PM on a Saturday night, lasting a few minutes, suggests the release of Thai lanterns following a festival. As the witness was observing westward, facing a light wind, the objects appeared motionless. The cornucopia shape was perceived due to a perspective effect of the lanterns, which were in fact almost aligned with the wind direction. Météociel reported a light westerly wind of around 10 km/h in Bordeaux: Weather. No other reports were collected. This case is classified as "B" – probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a red-orange object in the sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: Around 9:20 PM, a pedestrian's attention was drawn to a reddish-orange object that appeared to be on fire in the sky. The witness got into his car and drove directly under the object, which he then photographed. The object then deviated from its trajectory and disappeared from the witness's view. The Calsky observation does not mention any bright satellites at that time. There was a re-entry into the atmosphere of the TIROS2 satellite that day, but earlier in the day, which does not correspond at all to the observation. The witness's description, "a flame in the sky," suggests a Thai lantern, flying towards the southwest. The Météociel observation from Cannes indicates a light wind shifting from north to west between 9:00 PM and 10:00 PM. The direction of the object's movement could be consistent with the wind direction. The photos taken correspond well to the usual appearance of Thai lantern photos. The time and place (Sunday evening, during the Cannes Film Festival) are quite conducive to various festive events. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of a Thai lantern. The witness refutes this hypothesis.

summary: Observations of two waves of luminous balls moving silently across the sky: probable sightings of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 17, 2014 (not March 17, as mistakenly stated in his testimony), a witness and his wife were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Five or six red orbs appeared, coming from the northwest and moving towards the southeast. A second wave of about fifteen identical orbs was observed. Their slow movement was silent. This testimony is typical of a Thai lantern sighting: orange orbs moving slowly in a straight line at low altitude, carried by the wind on a weekend evening. The METEOCIEL weather report for Perpignan (weather) confirms the weakening northwesterly wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": a very probable observation of Thames lanterns. Given the low oddity of this observation, GEIPAN did not investigate the perpetrators of this sighting.

summary: Observation of a spherical white luminous phenomenon in the sky: certain sighting of a passenger plane approaching Nice airport.
description: On May 16, 2014, at 9:15 PM, a witness took two photographs of a spherical, white luminous phenomenon. The appearances and disappearances of the phenomenon intrigued him. The observation lasted 5 minutes. The witness sent us two photographs, but we did not receive the video also recorded during the observation. No other witness statements were reported. Given the evidence gathered during the investigation (see the investigation report), namely the azimuth measurement of the UFO intersecting the approach path of aircraft at Nice Airport, the altitude coinciding with that of approaching aircraft, and the observation distance allowing only the distinction of the landing light(s), the case is classified as "A," a confirmed sighting of an airliner approaching Nice Airport.

summary: Long observation with an onboard camera of a very bright UFO with scintillation: certain confusion with the star Antares.
description: On May 15, 2014, around 11:00 PM, the gendarmerie was patrolling with a helicopter over Lyon. An onboard camera filmed a bright UFO with strong scintillation for over 10 minutes. The stationary luminous object was visible to the naked eye for two and a half hours. Several parameters lead to the conclusion that it was mistaken for the star Antares (see the investigation report): - Long observation period, over two hours. - Fixed position in the sky. - Presence of strong scintillation clearly visible in the video, even when the point of light appears as an artifact (a truncated corona). At this low altitude, the scintillation of stars is often very pronounced. - Angular proximity of the Moon and the UFO, the latter being visible in the video. The strangeness of this case is low: it is mainly caused by the unusual appearance of the UFO, with its strong scintillation, as perceived by witnesses who had never used a camera to observe the sky before. The testimony is inconsistent, with relatively little data provided by the witness, but a video was made of the phenomenon and could be analyzed. This case is classified as an unidentified aerial phenomenon (UAE) due to a clear case of confusion with the star Antares.

summary: Observation of geometric shapes composed of points of light in silent movement: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation at 11:56 PM of orange orbs forming geometric shapes, crossing the sky in a few minutes, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. Their movement was observed from southwest, which is consistent with the northeast wind recorded at Roissy: Weather. No other reports were collected in the area. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation near a flying aircraft of a cigar-shaped phenomenon: certain observation of a shadow of the aircraft on a layer of non-condensed microparticles located at a nearby altitude.
description: The witness observed a cigar-shaped phenomenon near a passenger plane. He ruled out the possibility of a shadow and believed it to be a plane/UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) formation. Considering the information gathered in the attached investigation report, namely: - Relative positions of the witness, the plane, and the sun conducive to the formation of a shadow. - Other similar existing examples. - Movement in concert of the plane/UAP combination. - UAP slightly larger than a plane. - Presence of clouds in the immediate vicinity. This case is classified as A, as a confirmed observation of a shadow of the plane on a layer of uncondensed microparticles located at a nearby altitude.

summary: Observation of one or two silver balls by a pilot: lack of information.
description: Over the English Channel on May 13, 2014, at 5:35 PM (local time), a pilot reported to air traffic control an observation of a curious luminous phenomenon. He saw one or two silver balls on the left side of the aircraft. No other reports have been collected for this date. The very brief report simply mentions "one or two silver balls on the left" without specifying the duration or direction of the phenomenon. The sun was at an azimuth of 255°E (SW) at a height of 36°, to the right of the aircraft. The weather forecast for Caen indicated significant cloud cover. The reported phenomenon (silver ball) was on the left side of the aircraft. If the phenomenon was moving at the same speed as the aircraft, in the same direction, it could be a glory phenomenon (Brocken spectre, pilot's roundel) in the opposite direction to the sun, projected onto the cloud layer. It could also be atmospheric re-entry of space debris or a meteoroid. Due to a lack of detail in the witness statement, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" for insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous mass of fire-orange colour in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On May 12, 2014, at 10:26 PM, a mother and daughter were astonished to see a luminous, orange-flame mass moving across the sky. They initially thought it was a burning airplane or hot air balloon. However, the phenomenon moved calmly northeast without losing altitude and then disappeared, hidden by trees. The observation lasted one minute. Only one witness account was recorded. The observed luminous mass originated from Corbeil/Mennecy (south of Evry) and was heading towards Etioles/Tigery (east): it therefore appeared to be traveling in a northeast direction. The weather report Météociel indicates a light west wind (at 10 PM) to southwest wind (at 11 PM), and significant cloud cover (4 to 7/8): the object's movement is therefore consistent with the local wind. The color, duration, and mode of movement are consistent with a Thae lantern, probably licked by an individual after a celebration or as a test. However, the described shape (with orange rays) and the day (Monday) are unusual for a lantern. Another possible explanation is an aircraft approaching Orly Airport, preparing to enter the runways from the west (a head-on aircraft appears as a large, fixed point of light; flashing lights are not powerful enough to be visible under these conditions). The fact that the photograph taken by the witness yielded no results is not surprising: the Nintendo DS's camera is not sensitive enough for nighttime photography. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of a flashing white light crossing the sky from West to East: observation of the "Sinosat 2 Rocket" satellite.
description: On May 5, 2014, at 6:40 PM, a witness and a friend observed a flashing white light crossing the sky from west to east in 20 seconds. Only one witness account was recorded. The Calsky website indicated that same day at 6:33 PM, the "Sinosat 2 Rocket" satellite (the third stage that launched the Sinosat 2 satellite) passed over a west-to-east trajectory consistent with the observation. An observer of the same object, who posted their observation report online, indicated that "The photometric period is, visually, between 4 and 4.5 seconds" (see Sinosat documentation), which is consistent with the flashing reported by the witness (4 seconds of light, then 2 seconds without light). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as perfectly identified: observation of the "Sinosat 2 Rocket" satellite. It should be noted, however, that the observation period of 20 seconds is much shorter than the complete passage of the satellite which lasted 6 minutes, but the witness only observed it on the highest part of its trajectory (above 75th).

summary: Silent movement of several points of light forming a triangle: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The observation of white (or yellow) lights passing across the sky for a few minutes on a weekend night suggests the presence of Thai lanterns. In this case, the witness described a westward movement while the wind was blowing from north to south (recorded in Chartres). GEIPAN contacted the witness to clarify the movement of the objects: the witness described a movement along the axis of Rue des Frères Lumière, in its northeast/southwest section. The luminous objects were apparently moving southwest, which is more consistent with the northerly wind recorded in Chartres and Orléans. The color of Thai lanterns is most often described as yellow or orange, but, viewed from the side, the lanterns are sometimes perceived as white. It should be noted that another sighting of Thai lanterns occurred in Voves on June 27th at 10 PM, following a school celebration; a witness also described and photographed white lights. With all these elements, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of thae lanterns

summary: Observation of four white circles moving slowly through the clouds: lack of information.
description: On May 1, 2014, at 6:30 PM, a witness closed their window when they spotted four white circles moving very slowly and silently through the clouds towards the north, at an altitude of approximately 200 meters. The phenomenon quickly disappeared. No other reports were collected. Later that day, the witness reported seeing white circles within a white cloud. These could simply be gaps in the upper part of the cloud. This case is unusual and somewhat inconsistent due to the brevity and unique nature of the report, which lacks a photograph. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information.

summary: Observations of the silent movement of about ten yellow-orange luminous points in the night sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 28, 2014, at 10:00 PM, a couple in a car were intrigued by about ten bright lights in the sky. Yellow-orange orbs moved silently southward. The observation lasted three minutes before the orbs disappeared into the distance. A few photographs were taken with a cell phone. Two witness accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon. The police investigation did not uncover any specific events or other witnesses in the area that evening. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from north to south, then southwest, which is consistent with the north to northeast wind recorded in Bourg-lès-Valence. The Infoclimat report for Bourg-les-Valence indicates a light north-northeast wind (3 to 5 km/h). The significant elevation of Crussol Castle causes wind disturbances at low altitude, which could explain the change in direction. The witness took some photos: they turned out to be out of focus (a common issue with night photos under these conditions) or blurry. However, they confirm the reality of the phenomenon, and its color is entirely consistent with that of Thai lanterns. The witness's distance estimate cannot be accurate since he has never seen this type of object. Because Thai lanterns are inherently dim (large candle flame), they are always perceived as being farther away, and therefore larger and faster, than they actually are. See the explanation of estimating the size and distance of an unknown phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a very probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the north-south passage of two luminous phenomena in the sky (spherical shape for one and cigar-shaped for the other): observation of the passage of a satellite and a passenger plane.
description: On April 24, 2014, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness observed, from their balcony, the movement of a luminous white sphere followed by a second, elongated cigar-shaped object equipped with green and red lights and marked lengthwise by white lights. No sound was heard, which convinced the witness that it could not be an aircraft. No other witness statements were collected. This highly unusual and sufficiently plausible case appears to have been a case of mistaken identity involving an artificial satellite (specifically, the NOSS 3-6 Rocket) and a Boeing 737 or Airbus A330. Reconstructing the trajectories of these two objects shows that they correspond perfectly with those of UAPs (Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). Furthermore, the descriptions of UAPs perfectly match those of these two artificial objects. It is understandable that the witness did not recognize an aircraft during their observation, since any noise emanating from that aircraft could not have reached the witness due to the distance between them and the aircraft, as well as the wind being contrary to the direction of the PAN/witness. Similarly, the witness ruled out the possibility of an aircraft, as they were convinced that no aircraft was passing along the indicated trajectory, which is incorrect. The rather unusual and rapid co-occurrence (same trajectory, same altitude) of a satellite pass and a passenger plane could easily have created confusion, leading the witness to misidentify the two objects. This case is Class A: mistaken for a satellite and a passenger plane.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several white spherical shapes in the sky: lack of information.
description: On April 23, 2014, at 1:28 PM, a witness observing the clouds was intrigued by the passage of a white spherical shape followed by several others. The witness's account of small spherical objects moving beneath the cloud ceiling suggested the appearance of balloons being released. The Météociel weather station in Pau, very close to the observation site, indicated a change in wind direction that day, shifting from southeast at 10:00 AM to northwest at 2:00 PM, with increasing cloud cover. The wind at 1:30 PM was rather uncertain, blowing from the north to northwest. The wind was therefore highly variable at that time, but was blowing from the north-northwest at the time of observation, that is, in the opposite direction to the observed movement. No aircraft traffic was reported in this area on Flightradar24. The balloon hypothesis is not confirmed, unless one considers a more frequent variation in wind speed than the hourly readings. Due to a lack of simultaneous information on local wind conditions, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" in light of the uncertainty.

summary: Observation of the movement of three luminous yellow-orange balls in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 20, 2014, at 9:37 PM, a witness observed three luminous, yellow-orange orbs, larger than an airplane, moving along a south-south trajectory for two minutes. The orbs appeared incandescent and disappeared, leaving a trail. The witness took photographs. This observation is typical of Thai lantern sightings: orange orbs moving slowly in a straight line at low altitude, carried by the wind, on a weekend evening. The Météociel weather report for Melin confirms the light southerly wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": a very probable sighting of Thai lanterns. Given the low strangeness of this observation, GEIPAN did not investigate the perpetrators of this lick.

summary: Rapid appearance and disappearance of a black illuminated object during photographic shooting: probable observation of a passenger plane illuminated by the setting sun.
description: On April 16, 2014, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness was taking photos of birds when he noticed a peculiar, rapidly flashing light. He then observed a translucent black object through the camera lens, which did not appear in the photographs. No other witness statements were collected. Given the objective elements gathered in the investigation report—namely, conditions favorable to the creation of strong light reflections from parts of an airliner directed towards the witness, the presence of anti-collision and/or navigation lights, and the speed and distance of the unidentified flying object consistent with those of an airliner—we can conclude that the case involves the probable sighting of an airliner whose fuselage, or a part thereof, was strongly illuminated by the setting sun and reflected towards the witness. This case is classified as B, as a probable sighting of an airliner illuminated by the setting sun.

summary: Observation of the passage of three luminous objects advancing in formation in the sky: mistaken for the Yaogan 17 A, B and C satellite triplet.
description: On April 16, 2014, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness observed three luminous objects in the sky (between the constellations of Boötes and Virgo) from their home. These objects moved in formation before disappearing. A few seconds later, the witness observed a UFO resembling an atmospheric reentry. The witness estimated the total duration of the observation to be between 30 and 50 seconds. Only one witness report was collected. Of moderate strangeness and consistency (a single witness, but a precise report), this complex observation turned out to be a case of mistaken identity involving a specific trio of satellites: a triplet of Chinese military satellites, Yaogan 17 (see the investigation notes). The UFO exhibited all the typical characteristics of such a triplet: brightness, visual appearance, brief visibility due to a flash, and a perfectly consistent trajectory and time. The last part of the observation, which was not particularly strange, can be explained either by a meteor or by the flash from the Iridium 40 satellite that occurred that evening in Petit-Quevilly. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (observation of a particular type of satellite, simultaneous occurrence of two different phenomena). This case is classified as Class A, misinterpreted with the Yaogan 17 A, B, and C satellite triplet.

summary: Observation of a bright stationary object in the West sky: probable observation of the reflection of the setting sun on an airplane.
description: On April 10, 2014, around 6:00 PM, a witness observed a bright, stationary object in the sky. The observation lasted about thirty seconds, then the object disappeared instantly. Only one witness report was collected. A bright object observed in the west in the late afternoon suggests the reflection of the sun on an airplane or balloon. If it was an airplane, it must be a distant aircraft (more than 50 km away), heading in a direction close to that of the witness. The sudden disappearance is probably explained by a change in the object's orientation relative to the sun: it is the reflection that would have disappeared, but not the object itself. This somewhat unusual case is classified as "B," a probable observation of the reflection of the setting sun on a distant, high-altitude airplane (probable EZY434P according to Gasperflights).

summary: Observation of the silent movement of fluorescent green luminous points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 8, 2014, between 10:00 PM and 11:30 PM, a witness observed, through a partially open window, the silent, straight-line movement of a series of fluorescent green lights, connected by lines and extending for nearly 10 meters. The phenomenon was eventually obscured by nearby buildings. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness described the objects as being carried by the wind ("the impression of 'floating' in the air"). The wind measured in Avignon was from north to south, which is consistent with a movement perceived primarily as north to south, as it traveled from north-northwest to south-southeast. These are probably green Thai lanterns (lanterns can be of various colors and shapes (see the website Thai lanterns), possibly strung together (the light points appear as a line). Generally, such festive events take place on weekends, but celebrations are also possible during the week (a birthday?). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: Thai lanterns.

summary: Multiple observations in France of the passage of a luminous phenomenon in the night sky: observations of an atmospheric reentry.
description: On March 31, 2014, at approximately 10:33 PM, several people in different regions of France observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Three reports were collected, describing observations in Strasbourg (Bas-Rhin), Peigney (Haute-Marne), and Rombas (Moselle). That same day, numerous observations were recorded on specialized websites in France and also in Germany. The directions given by the witnesses correspond to the reconstructed trajectory of an atmospheric reentry. See the website amsmeteors. Consequently, GEIPAN classified it as an A event: meteoroid reentry.

summary: Observation of three luminous points, equidistant from each other and yellow-orange in color, moving silently in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 21, 2014, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness observed three equidistant, yellow-orange lights for two to three minutes. These lights moved silently along a straight path and suddenly accelerated before disappearing. The observation of these equidistant yellow-orange lights crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from east to west, which is consistent with the southerly wind shifting to west recorded in Marignane (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation). The perceived acceleration and disappearance is likely the witness's interpretation of the rapid decrease in brightness before the lantern was extinguished. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of three orange light points: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Thursday, March 20, 2014, at approximately 10:45 PM, two people observed three bright orange points in the sky. These points moved silently but rapidly in formation before disappearing one after the other. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of bright orange objects crossing the sky in a few minutes, carried by a light southerly wind (see weather in the evening, strongly suggests Thai lanterns. These lechers most often occur on Saturdays or Sundays. However, spring or Carnival may have provided an opportunity for a local festival: the Clesse town hall has not received any reports of this type of event. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Successive observations of several fixed, cylindrical, luminous objects in the sky: probable observations of stars by a witness with impaired vision.
description: On March 19, 2014, at 10:15 PM, a person closing their shutters saw several luminous, cylindrical objects in the sky (see the investigation report). The witness made other observations of this type. A neighbor also saw very bright lights in the sky, identical to stars. Only one witness statement was collected. Following the on-site investigation, it appears highly probable that the strange shapes observed by the witness were the result of vision problems (cataracts and presbyopia). As the observations were recurring, they should cease after the witness's cataract surgery scheduled for August 2014. Confirmation or refutation should also be provided by receiving the questionnaire from witness #2 (the neighbor). Pending either of these pieces of information, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observations of stars by a witness with impaired vision.

summary: Observation of four constant orange lights evoking a dark trapezoidal shape: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Tuesday, March 18, 2014, around 8:30 p.m., a couple out for a walk were surprised to see four steady, pale orange lights in the clear sky, resembling a dark trapezoidal shape. These lights moved silently at a constant speed along a straight path. The witness looked away, but the object had disappeared by the time they tried to see it again. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange lights flying silently, horizontally, in the same direction as the wind, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked after a festival. It is common to perceive a dark shape when observing several lights moving together (Gestalt effect). The witness saw the object move towards the East or Northeast: the wind reported at Lyon-Satolas was a light southwesterly wind, consistent with the observed movement: weather. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN did not investigate the person who made the lecher.

summary: Observation of the passage across the night sky of two large flying objects whose bases were formed by blue spheres: lack of information
description: On Saturday, March 15, 2014, at 11:43 PM, a witness observed the silent, successive passage of two large, identical objects flying over the roof of a supermarket. The witness described blue spheres, about the size of a soccer ball, spaced 3 to 4 meters apart at the base of these flying objects. The first object followed a straight trajectory, while the second object ascended and changed direction. They disappeared in different directions within seconds. The observation lasted 3 minutes. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the information gathered in the attached investigation report (see the investigation report), namely: - The number of UFOs in each formation is not specified. - The relative positions of the UFOs within the formations are not specified. - There are no angular measurements, either for the dimensions of the formations or for the individual UFOs. - The color of the UFOs is not specified. - Lack of detail regarding the UFO-shaped object resembling a large Boeing compared to the blue spheres. - Regarding the nightclub laser hypothesis, there is no data on the possible use of such equipment by the establishment in question during the evening of March 15, 2014. This lack of information prevents a definitive conclusion in favor of any hypothesis. This case is classified as C, as an observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state, due to a lack of factual elements and corroboration. This testimony is of weak consistency: imprecise, although accompanied by a diagram reproducing the observation, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly strange, as it could have involved entirely ordinary objects.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a bright white flash followed by a short white trail in the sky: observation of a bolide.
description: On March 14, 2014, at 7:30 p.m., a driver and his daughter observed a bright light moving very quickly across the cloudy sky through their windshield. The phenomenon disappeared below the horizon. The sighting of a large, very bright point, followed by a short trail, crossing part of the sky in about one second, suggests a fireball (the high-speed entry of a meteoroid, a small rocky body, into the atmosphere). This phenomenon was observed by many other witnesses who wrote on forums: Firebole of March 14, 2014 See also a video taken in Catalonia, Spain: Firebole in Spain. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" and identifies it as a firebole. See also: explanation: Firebole.

summary: Observation of the very slow and upward movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: astronomical observation of Venus.
description: From his south-facing window, a witness observed, on March 11, 2014, at 3:05 a.m., a very bright point to his left, therefore towards the East, slowly rising in the sky for 40 minutes. The diagram drawn by the witness places the phenomenon at an azimuth of 109°. The sky chart shows the planet Venus, bright in the morning sky at azimuth 107° at its rising (see the two charts produced by the Winstars software at 3:05 AM and 3:40 AM, in the direction indicated by the witness (109°)). GEIPAN classifies this case as 'A': observation of the planet Venus. The witness did not recognize Venus, perhaps because a celestial body on the horizon is often not recognized as a celestial body, but as an object flying over the landscape, but also because there were particular weather conditions that night: Infoclimat indicates a humidity of only 66%, therefore exceptional sky clarity, rare in this region (see weather report from March 10th to 11th. The other reports from that week indicate at least 76% humidity). If it had been a phenomenon other than Venus, the fact that the witness was looking exactly in the direction of On this planet, the witness would have seen the phenomenon ET Venus in the sky.

summary: Brief observation by a motorist of the passage in the sky of a dark tubular object with a green light: lack of information.
description: On March 10, 2014, between 7:30 PM and 7:45 PM, a motorist traveling at 110 km/h on the A63 motorway was intrigued by the movement of a black, tubular object against the blue sky. The UFO was about the size of a fairly thick fountain pen. The witness observed a small green light beneath the object, which seemed to accompany it during its straight trajectory. No unusual noise was heard during the continuous observation, which lasted less than three seconds. The object then moved out of the witness's field of vision, obscured by the landscape. The observation lasted one to two seconds. No other witness statements have been reported. Based on the evidence gathered in the case file, namely: - The UFO was moving against the prevailing wind. - Its appearance was consistent with that of an aircraft seen from the side. - A steady green light was present, which is inconsistent with the direction of flight of an aircraft. We can only conclude that the UFO observed by the witness cannot be easily characterized. Due to its similarity to an airplane and its straight trajectory, the strangeness of this observation is relatively low; the brevity of the observation, the unique nature of the testimony, and the fact that the witness was driving weaken the case. This case is classified as C due to a lack of corroborating evidence to support or refute either hypothesis (see the investigation report).

summary: Observation for three seconds of the straight passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky followed by a long and white trail: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On March 9, 2014, at 7:50 PM, a witness at home observed a faint phenomenon followed by a long, white trail in the sky for a few seconds. This observation of a luminous ball followed by a trail, crossing the sky in a straight line in 2 or 3 seconds, has all the characteristics of a bolide (see this term: bolide). The BOAM amateur network of automatic cameras (see BOAM Network) did not record this phenomenon, perhaps because it was not bright enough. However, two bolides were recorded that same evening, at 9:03 PM and 11:28 PM, by cameras located in eastern France. GEIPAN received a firsthand account of an observation made in Saint-André-de-Cubzac (33), near Bordeaux, on the same day between 7:30 and 7:45 PM, which could correspond to this phenomenon: the directions of movement of the phenomenon are consistent, but the reported observation times do not exactly coincide. Lacking confirmation, this case is currently classified as "B": probable observation of a fireball. Overall, numerous fireball observations were noted in February and March.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange diamond in the sky: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, March 9, 2014, at 12:28 AM, a witness observed from their apartment terrace the silent passage of an orange diamond shape across the sky. According to the witness, it moved at the speed of an airplane along a SE-NW trajectory. The observation of an orange object flying silently, horizontally, in the same direction as the wind, strongly suggests a sky lantern (Thai lantern or Tura balloon), probably released after a celebration. The witness saw the object depart towards the Northwest. The wind recorded in Bordeaux was a light Southeast wind: meteo. The diamond shape is unusual for Thai lanterns. It could also be a Tura balloon, which works on the same principle as a hot air balloon. See: Tura balloon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a flying lantern. GEIPAN did not investigate the lecher.

summary: Sighting of an orange crescent in the sky: observation of the Moon at its setting.
description: On March 7, 2014, between 12:25 and 12:40 AM, a person and their young daughter observed a yellow-orange crescent-shaped object in the sky. The witness instinctively took photographs. The photograph presented by the witness perfectly matches the shape of the Moon that day; it was a 34% first quarter. The Moon was indeed setting in the west-northwest (astronomical setting at 12:40 AM). It is surprising that the witness found this sight unusual and claims that the Moon rises and sets on the opposite side of their house! (Note: the Moon, like the Sun, always rises near the east and sets near the west). Perhaps it was the fear expressed by their young daughter at that late hour that moved the witness. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the Moon at its setting.

summary: Observation of the movement of a dark object in the shape of a horse flying in the sky: observation of a child's balloon.
description: On March 6, 2014, at 8:41 AM, a witness observed a dark, horse-shaped object in the sky that appeared to be rotating. He took photos and a video. The witness spotted the object 300 meters from his observation point. Analysis of the photos and the object's behavior are entirely consistent with a child's helium-filled balloon, shaped like a winged horse, such as those readily available here or here. This model is particularly popular for the "Year of the Horse" in the Chinese calendar. The shape is very clear in the photo, and you can even see the string that normally holds it to the ground. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as identified: child's balloon.

summary: Observation of numerous bright colored points of light in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: witness reported an observation made on March 2, 2014, at 7:40 PM concerning numerous white or yellow-orange luminous phenomena in the sky. The witness, who was driving to continue their observation, took a video and photographs with their cell phone. Only one witness account was collected for this phenomenon. The witness observed several luminous points that appeared stationary in the sky, the closest being blue-orange. One of them, higher than the others, disappeared behind the clouds. That day, Infoclimat's readings noted a light northerly wind, shifting to the south around 7:00 PM in Lyon, and around 9:00 PM in Valence. It is difficult to estimate the wind speed at 7:20 PM in Clonas, located between the two stations. See weather Bourg-lès-Valence and weather Lyon. The photos and videos are very similar to photos and videos of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long observation of a luminous phenomenon and observation in photos of overlapping luminous rectangles: photographic reflection.
description: On March 2, 2014, between 6:30 and 7:00 PM, a witness, while closing his shutters, observed a white luminous phenomenon moving slowly above the rooftops of the houses in the housing development. The witness took photographs before the phenomenon was obscured by trees. The observation lasted approximately thirty minutes. No other witness accounts were collected. The witness likely saw a light outside that surprised him that evening, prompting him to take out his camera. However, the strangeness underlying the testimony (and which is very likely its origin) lies in the rectangular and overlapping shape of the lights that the witness saw in the photos afterward. The witness's photos showing these lights clearly demonstrate framing through a glass door and highlight the luminous rectangles formed by reflections from the rectangular flash of the Minolta camera he was using. The light that caused the observation is barely described in the witness statement; the latter focuses on the rectangular oddity resulting from a photographic artifact. Consequently, GEIPAN concludes solely on what is described and constitutes the oddity experienced by the witness, classifying it as category A: photographic reflection.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a luminous phenomenon in the night sky; the phenomenon will make ascending and descending movements before disappearing: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On February 23, 2014, at 10:10 PM, a couple observed through a bay window the silent, straight passage of a very bright light. Suddenly, the phenomenon made several upward and downward movements, and the light turned red before disappearing in the direction of the west. The observation lasted between two and three minutes in the clear sky. The observation of an incandescent light with red reflections, moving horizontally across the sky for a few minutes, animated by small upward and downward movements, evokes the image of a Thai lantern carried by the wind, probably licked nearby after a private party. Meteociel forecasts heavy cloud cover (7/8) and an easterly wind of 17 to 28 km/h for Tours (see the weather). The wind direction is consistent with this hypothesis. However, it should be noted that lantern sightings are more frequent on Saturday evenings than on Sundays. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of two intersecting light phenomena: a misunderstanding with the ISS crossing the star Sirius during its trajectory.
description: On February 22, 2014, at approximately 7:45 PM, a resident of Marquette-lez-Lille (59) was returning home after shopping. As she parked in front of her house, she noticed a bright point of light moving to the left in the sky. After observing it for about two minutes, the UFO disappeared from the witness's field of vision, and she then went into her garden. She saw the UFO again and noticed a second one moving in the opposite direction. The two UFOs crossed paths. While the first continued to move away, the second stopped and remained stationary in the sky until clouds rolled in, between 10 minutes and an hour after the start of the observation. No other reports were collected. Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency (numerous coherent and precise details lending credibility to the case), this event appears to be a case of mistaken identity involving a well-known spacecraft, the International Space Station (ISS), crossing a particularly remarkable celestial body, the star Sirius, during its trajectory. The ISS was visible at a time very close to that given by the witness, on a trajectory perfectly consistent with that of the UFO. The close approach to Sirius during its trajectory could have given the illusion, for a short period of time, of the star moving in the opposite direction. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (fatigue, astonishment, observation in several phases). This case is classified as Class A: mistaken identity involving the ISS crossing Sirius during its trajectory.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a light followed by a trail: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid (meteorite fall).
description: The witness observed a very bright green light, followed by an orange trail, which crossed the sky in 3 to 4 seconds on February 22, 2014, at 8:10 PM. This phenomenon, called a bolide, was most likely caused by a meteoroid entering the atmosphere. The press reported the event: they saw the meteoroid in the sky, but no other witness reported the observation to GEIPAN. Nothing is reported on the BOAM website (cameras), but France was under cloud cover except in the southeast. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of an atmospheric entry of a meteoroid (meteoroid fall).

summary: Observations of the silent movement of several bright points in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On February 6, 2014, at 9:15 PM, a witness closing their shutters noticed several luminous objects moving silently across the sky. The observation of bright objects following one another in the sky, in the direction of the wind, is reminiscent of Thai lanterns. The witness observed the objects flying from north to south. The Météociel weather report for Bordeaux indicated a northwesterly wind of 22 to 33 km/h, partly cloudy (5/8). Given the wind direction, these lanterns could have been launched from the Quai des Chartrons. The Tet festival was celebrated in Bordeaux on February 8. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of the silent and slow passage of several orange lights in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 2, 2014, at 6:30 PM, two people observed the slow, silent passage of several orange lights in the sky. Only one witness report was filed. The sighting of orange orbs moving slowly across the sky, in the direction of the wind (South Wind, Force 11, 19 km/h recorded in Lille) on a weekend evening strongly suggested Thai lanterns (flying lanterns). See weather. The witness refuted this hypothesis. As the observation report is entirely consistent with this hypothesis, and given the frequency of lantern releases, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns. It should be noted that February 2nd is Candlemas, traditionally celebrated with torches or candles. GEIPAN, after a quick internet search, was unable to locate the perpetrators of the licking.

summary: Observation of the movement of a red luminous phenomenon with a small blue tail in the vicinity of the witness: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On January 28, 2014, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness outside observed a luminous UFO (Unidentified Floating Object) moving for two to three minutes. The object appeared as a halo, then as a very bright red sphere with a small blue tail. Its trajectory was complex: straight, then stopped, followed by a U-turn with a slight deviation, then back to a straight path in the opposite direction at the same altitude, before moving diagonally to the left and disappearing almost immediately into the sky. The object was first seen at a distance of 500 meters, then close to the witness (approximately 15 meters) before moving away again. Only one witness statement was recorded. An investigator met with the witness (see the investigation report). Given the unusual yet highly coherent nature of the witness's descriptions, and the spatiotemporal context of the phenomenon, which makes any human activity capable of explaining it highly improbable, it seems logical to acknowledge the current impossibility of providing a prosaic and reasoned explanation. Only an explanation based on the phenomenon of ball lightning, admittedly poorly understood but whose many facets seem to be emerging from the numerous testimonies collected over more than a century, could possibly account for the complex behavior of this event. There are indeed some similarities with certain lightning-related accounts (shape, size, color, brightness, slow, fluid movement close to the ground, sudden disappearance) that might suggest classifying this case in this category. However, there is no factual evidence to support this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as unexplained (category D1), because the description is detailed, the observation rather strange and made under good conditions.

summary: Observation by a motorist of the slow movement of three luminous orange shapes forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: On January 19, 2014, at 8:30 PM, a motorist on a highway observed three slowly moving orange luminous shapes in the sky, under which he was about to pass. He then saw an acute triangle. A very light wind, variable from south to east, was recorded: weather. The behavior of the objects is consistent with objects carried by the wind. The orange color evokes the color of Thai lanterns. However, the triangular shape described by the witness does not seem compatible with this hypothesis. (See GEIPAN photo DSC7031 of three Thai lanterns that could resemble what the witness saw). This testimony is of medium to weak consistency: the witness is driving his car and observing through the windshield; It is very difficult to estimate the actual movement of the objects, given that the witness is moving himself; GEIPAN has received no other reports of this phenomenon, even though the area is densely populated. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of corroborating evidence to either confirm or refute the hypothesis of Thai lanterns.

summary: Rapid observation of the passage of an intense light coming from a white ball and followed by a trail: observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On January 17, 2014, at 7:05 PM, a motorist on the D 6036 towards Saint-Bonnet-du-Gard (30) was surprised to see a powerful light, originating from a white sphere followed by a trail, pass across the sky for a few seconds. No unusual noise was heard. No other reports were filed with GEIPAN. This very bright phenomenon was observed simultaneously across much of eastern France, especially in the Northeast (Alsace, Lorraine, Vosges), by numerous witnesses and at least four automatic cameras located in Chaligny, Bollwiller, Val d'Ajol, and at the Paris Observatory (see attachments). The east-to-west trajectory was clearly described by all witnesses. As is often the case, witnesses had the impression of a very close phenomenon, even though these fireballs occur at altitudes of 100 to 40 or 30 km. The characteristics of this fireball (duration, westward trajectory) are those of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid, a small stony body, probably originating from the asteroid belt. The parameters recorded by the BOAM network cameras in northeastern France allowed the following characteristics of the fireball to be established: AllSkyCamFrance "The "unified" trajectory given by the UFOorbit software is similar to the northernmost one (from Verdun to Reims): Vg (speed): 14 km/s, duration: 6.1 s, maximum magnitude (from Chaligny): -7, absolute magnitude: -5.5, start > altitude: 87 km, latitude: 49.08eN, longitude: 5.49eE; end > altitude: 38 km, latitude: 49.20eN, longitude: 4.09°E, inclination: 25°, distance traveled: 115 km. The fireball appeared to the witness in a N-NE direction, at an elevation (above the horizon) calculated to be between 5° and 2° (taking into account the Earth's curvature), which corresponds well to the diagram produced by the witness. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. This object may have been large enough to produce a meteorite that landed on the ground in western France.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a luminous white ball in the sky: probable observation of a bolide.
description: Through the bay window of their living room, the witnesses saw a very bright, luminous ball pass by in two seconds. This description alone already suggests the observation of a bolide, that is, the entry of a meteor into the atmosphere. The luminous ball had a slight trail. GEIPAN received no other reports, and the BOAM website (Meteor Observer Database) did not record this type of event at that time. This testimony is very consistent due to the two witnesses and the precision of the description of the phenomenon's trajectory. The intuitive altitude estimate (100m) is very likely incorrect, as is the case with all unknown phenomena: in this instance, because the phenomenon was very bright, the witness interpreted it as very close, but without objective reference points. The very clear sky allowed the phenomenon to be highly visible, and thus perceived as even closer. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a fireball. NB: Because the witness observed the phenomenon through a window, GEIPAN also considered the hypothesis of an artificial light (motorcycle headlight, electric torch) coming from behind the witnesses, but the fields of view do not seem to correspond to the directions of observation.

summary: Observation of a colored trail in the sky: observation of an airplane condensation trail.
description: This observation, made on January 11, 2014, at 4:50 PM, and the associated photograph, exhibit all the characteristics of an aircraft contrail observed at sunset. See the GEIPAN information on this subject: aircraft contrails. The FlightRadar data shows intense air activity within the witness's field of view: several aircraft are candidates for having produced this condensation trail. The weather report weather. The report indicates a northerly wind with excellent visibility of 60 km. The observed contrail is probably 100 to 120 km away, visible due to its altitude (10,000 m) and especially the lighting conditions provided by the setting sun. It is likely that these excellent weather conditions, and an unusual vantage point, are what surprised the witness of this rather common phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of an aircraft contrail. For your information: comets are only visible at night, as their contrails are faint.

summary: Quick observation of the silent passage of 8 luminous shapes appearing successively in the sky: probable observation of birds in flight at high altitude.
description: On January 11, 2014, at approximately 4:25 PM, a witness observed the moon in a cloudy sky when he saw up to eight bright white lights appear, silently rotating, and disappear from his sight after a few minutes in a straight line. The observation lasted 15 seconds. No other witness statements were collected. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report—namely, the presence of a clear and bright sky and good visibility, the low position of the sun on the horizon and the contrast effect, the UFOs being in a spatial configuration favorable to their visibility by the witness (strong reflection of sunlight), and the visible shape of the UFOs—we can conclude that all the conditions were met for the witness to have observed simple white birds flying at high altitude, strongly reflecting sunlight back at him. This case is to be classified as B as a probable observation of birds in flight at high altitude.

summary: Quick observation between two clouds of a bright white object: observation of the reflection of the sun on an aircraft.
description: On January 9, 2014, at 9:35 a.m., a witness, driving their car, glimpsed a bright, white object in the sky between the clouds for three-quarters of a second. The witness, on the A6 motorway, heading from the provinces towards Paris, was therefore facing due north. The Casperflights commercial flight data recorder indicated that at 9:37 a.m., flight AF620 JL (Airbus A321) was climbing between 2,500 and 3,000 meters after taking off from Roissy Airport. This aircraft was ideally oriented so that its fuselage reflected the rising sun towards the observer. The wings, being horizontal, did not reflect the sun and were therefore barely visible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the sun's reflection on an aircraft.

summary: Observation of several diffuse luminous phenomena moving in the clouds above Paris: probable observation of the impact of laser beams on the cloud layer.
description: On the evening of January 7, 2014, between 8:00 PM and 11:00 PM, a person observed, from their home, successively diffuse and moving luminous phenomena in the cloudy sky above Paris. The phenomenon moved in an arc of varying length, sometimes pausing for a second. Only one witness statement was collected, and two photos were included with the questionnaire. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report—namely, the movement, color, shape, and diffuse appearance of the UFOs, the entirely plausible and explainable absence of a beam, and the presence of facilities along the observation's azimuth likely to use such equipment—we can conclude that the observed UFOs were probably simply laser impacts on the lower, dense cloud layer. This case is classified as B, as a probable observation of laser beam impacts used in a localized event on the cloud layer.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent evolutions of about fifteen blue or white lights in the sky: probable observation of a laser animation.
description: witness reported seeing about fifteen blue or white lights in the sky, looking south of Le Grand-Bornand (towards La Clusaz, located behind the Danay mountain) on January 7, 2014, around 10 p.m. The "Le Bal" nightclub in La Clusaz has a laser and uses it every night, even on weekdays. This establishment is located approximately 4 km south of the observation point. The laser projected a white spot that rapidly traced circles in the sky. The fact that the observation ceased when the sky cleared strengthens the hypothesis that it was this laser, projected onto the clouds, that the witness observed. The witness, a regular visitor to the area, believes that what he saw was not a nightclub laser. The police report notes that the witness had taken IXPRIM that day, a painkiller containing Tramadol, known to rarely cause hallucinations (between 1/100 and 1/100). The witness's perception may have been impaired by medication. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a laser projection from a nightclub onto clouds.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of two anthracite grey cylindrical objects in a cloud break: probable observation of the passage of two airliners in a cloud break.
description: On January 3, 2014, at approximately 3:10 PM, a driver and his passenger were intrigued by the slow passage, through a break in thick clouds, of two cigar-shaped, dark gray objects. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the evidence gathered during the investigation (see investigation report), the altitude, height, azimuths, and distance of the UFOs from the witnesses are consistent with those of aircraft suspected of being responsible for the sighting. We can conclude that the UFOs observed by the witness were likely just two airliners seen under specific conditions. These two aircraft were flights AFR1263 and AFR1471. This witness statement is fairly consistent: quite precise, but without photographs and coming from a single witness. A summary diagram drawn by the witness proved useful in this case. The observation is quite strange because it involves objects with seemingly unusual behavior. However, due to uncertainty about the time the planes passed and the angular size of the objects reported by witnesses, this case is classified as B, meaning a very probable sighting of two airliners.

summary: Observation of the straight and silent passage of about twenty red luminous points in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2014, at approximately 12:08 AM, a witness on their balcony observed the silent movement of numerous bright red objects in the sky, moving in a straight line across the cloudy sky. This observation of 23 bright red points flying linearly along the same trajectory has all the characteristics of Thai lanterns, very commonly released at the end of the holidays. The New Year's occasion reinforces this hypothesis. The weather report notes a light southerly wind (southwest at 11 PM, south at midnight, southeast at 1 AM). See: weather. Although the witness denies that these were sky lanterns, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of Thai lanterns. The low oddity of this type of sighting on January 1st at midnight does not warrant a field investigation.

summary: Observation of several luminous orange balls passing in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2014, at approximately 1:10 AM, a witness in the street observed five luminous, yellow-orange orbs passing successively across the cloudy sky. The observation lasted about twenty minutes before the orbs disappeared one after the other. No other accounts were collected. This very precise and well-documented account describes the passage of five luminous orbs with a yellow-orange glow. Their horizontal trajectory was straight, and the objects moved below the cloud cover. The wind recorded in Pontoise-Cormeilles was from the southwest. The Infoclimat report for Saint-Ouen-L'Aumène indicated a south-southwest wind. The witness looks southeast and sees the orbs moving from his right to his left as they rise. He has the impression that the orbs are approaching each other, whether this is actually happening or due to an increase in their brightness. The videos, excessively zoomed and out of focus (focus blur), do not show the details of the object, only its orange color and various optical and digital artifacts. The trajectory of the lights as proposed in the report compiled by the witness is not substantiated.
